definition_zh: 安排；布置；排列；布局；协议；筹备事项；改编曲；编配；（债务）和解安排
definition_en: the act of putting things or plans in order, the order or layout that results, an agreed plan between parties, and a piece of music reworked for particular voices or instruments
core_image: 长桌上，椅子被摆成两列，花球按高矮排好，流程表上的时刻一格一格对齐——同一双手先排物，再排事，最后排出一纸约定
scene: The wedding planner taps her clipboard and says: The seating arrangement is done, the flowers arrive at noon, and the band starts at six.
sceneCN: 这里 arrangement 是「布置」（第 2 个义项：物品摆放或装饰的方式）；句意：座位已经排好，花中午送到，乐队六点开场。画面里有写字板、成排椅子和一束尚未插好的花。

pos.zh: 安排；布置；排列；布局；协议；改编曲

senses.title: The act of setting things in order
senses.titleCN: 安排：把物与事一件件排进次序
senses.definition: the act of putting things or plans into a particular order, or of preparing for something
senses.definitionCN: 把事物或计划排成一定次序、为某事做准备的行为
senses.example: The arrangement of the furniture took the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 摆放家具花了整个下午。
senses.why: The noun is borrowed in 1740 from French arrangement, from arranger. Its base verb first meant 'draw up a line of battle' in the late 14c., so the noun starts as the act of lining things up — and a plan is only a line-up of steps.
senses.whyCN: 名词于 1740 年从法语 arrangement 借入，来自 arranger。其动词在 14 世纪末原义是“排开阵线”，所以名词起初就是“把东西排成线”的动作——而计划不过是一串排好队的步骤。

senses.title: The look of a thing once placed
senses.titleCN: 布置：摆好之后眼前的那个样子
senses.definition: the way in which things are placed or decorated; a display
senses.definitionCN: 物品摆放或装饰的方式；陈设
senses.example: She admired the arrangement of white lilies in the glass bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 她欣赏玻璃碗里白百合的插法。
senses.why: The 1800 sense 'that which is put in order, combination of parts or materials' turns the action into its visible result. When the hand stops, the order stays on the table as something to look at.
senses.whyCN: 1800 年的义项“被排好的东西、部件或材料的组合”把动作变成了可见的结果。手停下来之后，那个次序就留在桌上，成为一件可看的东西。

senses.title: Order in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 排列：谁先谁后，按一条规则站队
senses.definition: the order in which items are placed in a series, as alphabetical or chronological arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 事物在序列中的次序，如按字母或时间排列
senses.example: The files are kept in alphabetical arrangement.
senses.exampleCN: 这些档案按字母顺序排列。
senses.why: A row need not run across a table; it can run along the alphabet or along time. Because the root rang meant 'rank', arrangement can name any rule-governed sequence, not only a physical display.
senses.whyCN: 一排不必横在桌面上，也能沿字母表或时间延伸。因为词根 rang 本义是“行列”，arrangement 可以指任何按规则排出的序列，而不只是实物的陈列。

senses.title: The plan of the whole
senses.titleCN: 布局：各部分怎样凑成一个整体
senses.definition: the structure or organization of the parts of something, such as a room, a poem or a garden
senses.definitionCN: 某物各部分的结构或组织方式，如房间、诗歌或花园
senses.example: The arrangement of the chapters makes the argument easy to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 章节的布局让论证容易跟上。
senses.why: The 1800 'combination of parts' sense is spatial first, then structural: when the parts are seen as one whole, their placement becomes design. A poem's arrangement is its architecture.
senses.whyCN: 1800 年“部件的组合”义起初是空间性的，随后变成结构性的：当部分被看成一个整体，它们的位置就成了设计。一首诗的 arrangement 就是它的建筑结构。

senses.title: A deal between people
senses.titleCN: 协议：双方把各自的条件排到同一条线上
senses.definition: a plan or agreement made between two or more people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 两人或两方之间订立的计划或协议
senses.example: We have an arrangement with the landlord to pay the rent quarterly.
senses.exampleCN: 我们与房东约定按季度付房租。
senses.why: The sense 'final settlement, adjustment by agreement' is recorded in 1855. Two parties shift their positions until the rows meet; the result is an arrangement, a joint line-up rather than a quarrel.
senses.whyCN: “经协商的最终了结”义记录于 1855 年。双方挪动各自的立场，直到两排对齐；结果就是一项 arrangement——一条共同排出的线，而不是一场争吵。

senses.title: Things already settled
senses.titleCN: 筹备事项：一件件排进日程
senses.definition: (plural) plans or preparations made for a future event
senses.definitionCN: （复数）为将来某事所做的计划或准备
senses.example: I've made all the arrangements for the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 会议的一切我都安排好了。
senses.why: The action noun pluralizes naturally: every item to be placed in order is one arrangement. Travellers speak of arrangements because a journey is a row of fixed pieces — tickets, rooms, times.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词天然可以变复数：每一件要排进次序的事就是一个 arrangement。旅行者说 arrangements，因为旅程就是一排固定的小块——票、房间、时间。

senses.title: Notes reworked for new players
senses.titleCN: 改编曲：把曲子重新排给另一批人唱奏
senses.definition: a piece of music adapted for instruments or voices other than those it was written for
senses.definitionCN: 为原曲未曾预设的乐器或声部改写的乐曲
senses.example: The choir sang a choral arrangement of the folk song.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团唱了这首民歌的合唱改编版。
senses.why: The musical sense appears by 1813, defined as adapting a composition to voices or instruments 'for which it has not been designed'. The notes are literally re-lined-up, part by part.
senses.whyCN: 音乐义于 1813 年出现，定义为把作品改编给“它原本并非为之写作的声部或乐器”。音符被逐声部地重新排了一遍。

senses.title: Giving each instrument its line
senses.titleCN: 编配：把音符一排排分给各声部
senses.definition: the act or result of assigning the parts of a piece to particular instruments or voices
senses.definitionCN: 把乐曲各声部分配给特定乐器或声部的工作或结果
senses.example: The arranger's string arrangement turns the melody into a conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 编曲者的弦乐编配把旋律变成了一场对话。
senses.why: This is the craft behind the previous sense: the same row-image, now applied to the vertical stack of parts. Assigning one line to each instrument is arranging in the strictest sense, which is why the person is called an arranger.
senses.whyCN: 这是上一个义项背后的手艺：同一个“排”的意象，此刻用在纵向叠起的声部上。把一条线分给一件乐器，就是最严格意义上的 arranging，所以那个人被叫作 arranger。

senses.title: Claims put in order
senses.titleCN: 和解安排：债主与债户把账排成一个了结方案
senses.definition: a legal or financial settlement in which debts or claims are adjusted by agreement, as a scheme of arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 通过协议调整债务或请求权的法律或财务了结方案，如债务和解方案
senses.example: The company reached an arrangement with its creditors to repay over five years.
senses.exampleCN: 公司与债权人达成为期五年的还款和解安排。
senses.why: The 1855 'settlement by agreement' sense grew a legal branch: creditors' claims are lined up, reduced and scheduled. English law calls it a scheme of arrangement — an order imposed on a chaos of debt.
senses.whyCN: 1855 年“经协议了结”的义项长出一个法律分支：债权人的请求被排成队、削减并排期。英国法称之为 scheme of arrangement——给一团乱账排出的次序。

intro.en: Arrangement is a French noun built on a Germanic row. The verb reached English around 1400 as a military term; the noun arrived in 1740, and from 'putting in order' it spread to furniture, plans, contracts, music and debts.
intro.cn: arrangement 是一个建立在日耳曼语“排”之上的法语名词。动词约在 1400 年以军事术语进入英语；名词 1740 年才到来，并从“排好次序”扩散到家具、计划、契约、音乐和债务。

items.en: The root *sker- (2) 'to turn, bend' is the reconstructed source of Proto-Germanic *hringaz 'something curved, a circle'. No PIE text survives, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *sker-（第 2 义）“转、弯”是原始日耳曼语 *hringaz“弯曲之物、圆圈”的重构来源。没有 PIE 书面记录，这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Frankish *hring 'ring' gave Old French rang 'rank, row'; rangier meant 'set in a row' and arengier 'put in a row, draw up in battle order'. A ring of people seen from the side is a line, and the line became the word.
items.cn: 法兰克语 *hring“环”给出古法语 rang“行列”；rangier 义为“排成行”，arengier 义为“排成行、排成战斗队形”。一圈人从侧面看就是一条线，这条线成了词义。

items.en: The verb is recorded as arengen 'draw up a line of battle'. It stayed rare until the sense generalized to 'place things in order' around 1780–1800; 'come to an agreement' follows by 1786 and the musical 'adapt' by 1808.
items.cn: 动词记录为 arengen“排开阵线”。它一直罕用，直到约 1780–1800 年泛化为“把东西排好”；“达成一致”于 1786 年出现，音乐上的“改编”于 1808 年出现。

items.en: The noun is borrowed from French arrangement (Old French arengement), 'act of putting in proper order'. Its -ment continues Latin -mentum through French, a suffix that names the result or the means of an action as well as the action itself.
items.cn: 名词从法语 arrangement（古法语 arengement）借入，义为“排好次序的行为”。它的 -ment 经法语承自拉丁 -mentum，这个后缀既指动作，也指动作的结果或手段。

items.en: 'That which is put in order, a combination of parts or materials' is recorded in 1800, and the musical sense — adapting a composition to voices or instruments it was not designed for — in 1813.
items.cn: “被排好之物、部件或材料的组合”记录于 1800 年；音乐义——把作品改编给原本并非为其写作的声部或乐器——记录于 1813 年。

items.en: 'Final settlement, adjustment by agreement' is recorded in 1855. Later legal usage turns it into a scheme of arrangement for debts, while business and education borrow the noun without changing the row-image inside it.
items.cn: “经协议达成的最终了结”记录于 1855 年。后来的法律用法把它变成债务和解方案，而商业与教育借走这个名词时，里面的“排”意象并没有改变。

note.en: The first group collects words that look close but mostly come from other roots; only range and rank are true kin. The second group shares the idea of an order or a deal, not the spelling.
note.cn: 第一组收的是形近词，但它们多半另有词源；只有 range 与 rank 是真正的同族。第二组共享“次序或约定”的观念，而不是拼写。

entries.definition: a formal charge read out in court. It comes from Old French araisnier (ad- + raison 'reason, account'), not from the row-root.
entries.definitionCN: 刑事传讯；正式宣读指控。它来自古法语 araisnier（ad- + raison“理、辩解”），与“排”的词根无关。

entries.definition: a row, a span or a line of mountains. Arrange is literally a- plus range, to set in a row.
entries.definitionCN: 一排；范围；山脉。arrange 字面就是 a- 加 range，即“排成行”。

entries.definition: a line of soldiers or a position in an order; the same Germanic row without -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 行列；等级；同一日耳曼语“排”，只是没有 -ment。

entries.definition: the running of an organization. It joins -ment to manage, from Italian maneggiare 'handle, train horses', from manus 'hand'.
entries.definitionCN: 管理；经营。它把 -ment 加在 manage 上，后者出自意大利语 maneggiare“操控、驯马”，再上溯拉丁 manus“手”。

entries.definition: the way things are arranged one after another. Latin ordo also meant 'row', so the two words circle the same image from different roots.
entries.definitionCN: 顺序；命令。拉丁 ordo 也指“一排”，两个词从不同词源绕着同一个意象转。

entries.definition: the way parts are laid out on a page or in a space; it matches arrangement as visible result.
entries.definitionCN: 版面或空间的布局；对应 arrangement 的“可见结果”义。

entries.definition: a mutual understanding between parties. It overlaps arrangement in the sense of a settled deal.
entries.definitionCN: 协议；一致。它在“已达成的约定”义上与 arrangement 重叠。

entries.definition: something altered to suit a new purpose, especially a piece of music or a text.
entries.definitionCN: 为适应新用途而改写之物，尤指乐曲或文本。

entries.definition: the arrangement of parts, and also a person's habitual temper. Latin disponere 'set in different places' supplies both.
entries.definitionCN: 布置；性情。拉丁 disponere“分置各处”同时供给了这两层意思。

normalIntro.en: The family is one row seen from several angles: chairs, flowers, notes, dates and debts are all lined up.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族就是从几个角度看同一排：椅子、花、音符、日期、债务，全都被排成线。

normal.en: arrange = a- + range: to arrange is to put something into a range, a row.
normal.cn: arrange = a- + range：arrange 就是把东西放进一排。

normal.en: -ment turns the act into a thing: you arrange, and what is left on the table is an arrangement.
normal.cn: -ment 把动作变成东西：你 arrange，桌上留下的就是 arrangement。

normal.en: A floral arrangement, a seating arrangement and a musical arrangement are all rows — of flowers, chairs and notes.
normal.cn: 花艺布置、座位安排、音乐改编都是排——花、椅子、音符的排。

normal.en: An arrangement with the band is a row of agreed terms, not a row of objects.
normal.cn: 与乐队的 arrangement 是一排商定的条件，不是一排实物。

normal.en: Arraignment looks like arrangement but belongs to raison, 'reason', not to rows.
normal.cn: arraignment 形似 arrangement，却属于 raison“理”，与“排”无关。

abstract.en: Ordering is human: the row does not exist in nature until a hand lays it out.
abstract.cn: 排是人的动作：在有一只手摆开之前，自然界里并没有这一排。

abstract.en: Agreement is two rows brought into one line; settlement is that line made legal.
abstract.cn: 协议是把两排并成一排；和解是让这一排具有法律效力。

abstract.en: Every arrangement is a promise about where things will be: chairs, notes, money, days.
abstract.cn: 每一项 arrangement 都是关于“东西将在哪里”的承诺：椅子、音符、钱、日子。

examples.en: The seating arrangement for the dinner had to be changed twice.
examples.cn: 晚宴的座位安排不得不改了两次。

examples.en: They came to an arrangement that satisfied both companies.
examples.cn: 他们达成了一项两家公司都满意的协议。

examples.en: He wrote a jazz arrangement of the old hymn for the school band.
examples.cn: 他为校乐队把这首老赞美诗写成了爵士改编曲。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: a（向）+ range（一排）+ ment（名词）——把东西排成一排、把事排成一串，就是“安排、布置”；排定的条款成了“协议”。

root: 源自法语 arrangement ← arranger ← 古法语 arengier（a-“向”+ rangier“排成行”），rang“行列”出自法兰克语 *hring、原始日耳曼语 *hringaz“环、弯曲之物”；与 range、rank 同族，核心是“排成一行”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one image: a row made by a hand. The hand lays out chairs and flowers, then steps, then terms, then notes, and finally debts — each row is a different material, the act is the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守住同一个意象：人手排出的一行。手先排椅子与花，再排步骤，再排条款，再排音符，最后排债务——每一排材料不同，动作却是同一个。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of chairs brought into line by a hand that also lines up the schedule.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手把两排椅子摆齐，也把日程排齐。

chain: THE ORDER LEFT ON THE TABLE

branches.en: THE HAND AND WHAT IT LEAVES: the act of ordering, and the visible order that remains.
branches.cn: 手与它留下的东西：排的动作，以及留下的可见次序。

branches.en: SEQUENCE AND STRUCTURE: an order along a rule, and the plan of the whole.
branches.cn: 序列与结构：按规则排出的顺序，以及整体的布局。

branches.en: WHAT IS AGREED AND WHAT IS PREPARED: a deal between parties, and the items already scheduled.
branches.cn: 约定的与备好的：双方达成的协议，以及已排进日程的事项。

branches.en: THE MUSICAL ROW: a work reworked for new performers, and the scoring of its parts.
branches.cn: 音乐的一排：为新的演唱者改写的作品，以及各声部的编配。

branches.en: THE DEBTOR'S ROW: claims lined up, reduced and scheduled into a settlement.
branches.cn: 债户的一排：债权被排队、削减、排期，成为一个了结方案。

intro.en: Arrangement is built by suffixation: a borrowed verb plus -ment, then further prefixes (re-, pre-, dis-). The base rang is Germanic, though the suffix -ment is Latin by way of French.
intro.cn: arrangement 靠加后缀构成：借来的动词加 -ment，再加前缀（re-、pre-、dis-）。词根 rang 属日耳曼语，而 -ment 是经法语来的拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin: -mentum, through French -ment. The row-root rang comes from Frankish and Proto-Germanic; the a- of arrange continues Latin ad- 'to' but entered French first.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁的：-mentum 经法语 -ment 而来。“排”的词根 rang 出自法兰克语与原始日耳曼语；arrange 的 a- 承自拉丁 ad-“向”，但先进了法语。

items.meaning: the act of ordering, or the order produced
items.meaningCN: 安排的动作，或排出的次序
items.example: The arrangement of the desks follows no rule at all.
items.exampleCN: 这些课桌的摆放完全没有规则。

items.structure: a- (ad-, to) + rangier (set in a row)
items.meaning: to set in order; to adapt music
items.example: She arranged the chairs in a semicircle.
items.exampleCN: 她把椅子排成半圆形。

items.meaning: one who orders or adapts music
items.example: The arranger kept the melody but changed the harmony.
items.exampleCN: 编曲者保留了旋律，却改了和声。

items.meaning: a new ordering of what was already ordered
items.example: A rearrangement of the desks gave the room more light.
items.exampleCN: 重新摆放课桌让房间更亮。

items.meaning: an ordering fixed in advance
items.example: The visit was a prearrangement made months earlier.
items.exampleCN: 这次访问是几个月前预先安排好的。

items.meaning: to undo an order; to make untidy
items.example: The wind disarranged the neat rows of papers.
items.exampleCN: 风把排得整齐的文件吹乱了。

items.meaning: a state of lost order
items.example: The disarrangement of the shelves took a week to fix.
items.exampleCN: 货架的混乱花了一周才整理好。

items.structure: Old French rang (row), same root, no suffix
items.meaning: a row, a span, a stretch of ground
items.example: A range of hills closes the valley.
items.exampleCN: 一道山丘封住了山谷。

items.meaning: a line, a grade or position
items.example: The soldiers stood in two ranks.
items.exampleCN: 士兵站成两列。

latinEntries.meaning: noun suffix for the result or means of an action
latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示动作结果或手段的名词后缀

latinEntries.structure: Latin ad 'to', reduced to a- in French

definition_zh: 人造的；人工的；假的；虚假的；做作的；人为的；人工繁育的；（法律）拟制的
definition_en: made by human skill rather than by nature, and hence often standing in for something natural, not genuine, or not spontaneous
core_image: 暖房里，一株兰花的根泡在配好的营养液里，灯管替太阳值班，花梗被支架撑成理想的角度——自然的样子，全部由技艺做成
scene: A lab guide points at the case and says: This orchid is artificial, though it looks almost real under the lamp.
sceneCN: 这里 artificial 是「人造的」（第 1 个义项：由人制造而非自然生成的）；句意：这株兰花是人造的，尽管在灯下看起来几乎是真的。画面里有玻璃罩、灯管和一张宣传海报。

pos.zh: 人造的；人工的；假的；虚假的；做作的；人为的

derivatives.zh: 人工地；人为地；不自然地

senses.title: Made by human hands, not grown
senses.titleCN: 人造的：不是长出来的，是做出来的
senses.definition: made by people rather than occurring naturally, especially of materials or objects
senses.definitionCN: 由人制造而非自然生成的，尤指材料或物品
senses.example: The field is covered with artificial turf.
senses.exampleCN: 这块场地铺着人造草皮。
senses.why: Latin artificialis meant 'of or belonging to art', and ars is skill, not nature. A thing whose form comes from ars plus facere, 'to make', is made rather than grown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 artificialis 义为“属于技艺的”，而 ars 是技艺，不是自然。一个形态来自 ars 加 facere“做”的东西，是被做出来的，不是长出来的。

senses.title: Supplied by technique, not by nature
senses.titleCN: 人工的：本该由自然提供，却由技术提供
senses.definition: produced by human technique to take the place of a natural process, as artificial light or artificial rain
senses.definitionCN: 以人工技术替代自然过程而产生的，如人工光、人工降雨
senses.example: Seedlings are raised under artificial light in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天，幼苗在人工光照下培育。
senses.why: From the 16c. the word was applied to whatever imitates or substitutes for something natural. When the natural source — sun, rain — is absent, technique steps in.
senses.whyCN: 自 16 世纪起，这个词被用在任何模仿或替代自然之物上。当自然来源——太阳、雨水——缺席时，技术就补上。

senses.title: A stand-in for the real thing
senses.titleCN: 假的：顶替真东西的那一件
senses.definition: an imitation or substitute for something natural, as artificial teeth or artificial flowers
senses.definitionCN: 对自然之物的模仿或替代品，如假牙、假花
senses.example: She wore an artificial rose in her hair.
senses.exampleCN: 她头上戴了一朵假玫瑰。
senses.why: A substitute must be shaped like what it replaces. Sixteenth-century usage attaches the word to teeth, flowers and tears — things that look real precisely because they were made to.
senses.whyCN: 替代品必须做得像它所替代的东西。16 世纪的用法把这个词系在牙齿、花和眼泪上——它们看起来真，恰恰因为是被照着做出来的。

senses.title: Invented rather than true
senses.titleCN: 虚假的：被编出来当成真的
senses.definition: fictitious, assumed, not genuine
senses.definitionCN: 虚构的、假定的、不真实的
senses.example: The report gives an artificial picture of steady growth.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告描绘出一幅虚假的稳步增长图景。
senses.why: The 1640s sense 'fictitious, assumed' extends 'made by man' to statements: a fabricated account has a maker, not a source.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪 40 年代“虚构的、假定的”义把“人造”扩展到陈述上：编造出来的说法有一个制造者，却没有来源。

senses.title: Manufactured behaviour
senses.titleCN: 做作的：表情也是做出来的
senses.definition: insincere, affected, lacking spontaneity
senses.definitionCN: 不真诚的、做作的、缺乏自然流露的
senses.example: His artificial enthusiasm made the audience uncomfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 他做作的热情让观众不自在。
senses.why: The 1590s sense 'full of affectation' applies the word to manner. The earliest English sense, late 14c., was already 'not natural or spontaneous'; a smile can be manufactured like a flower.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 90 年代“充满做作”的义项把这个词用到举止上。英语最早（14 世纪末）的义项本就是“非自然的、非自发的”；笑容可以像花一样被制造。

senses.title: Bred or fertilized by technique
senses.titleCN: 人工繁育的：把自然那一步交给技术
senses.definition: of breeding, fertilization or incubation carried out by human technique rather than naturally
senses.definitionCN: 以人工技术而非自然方式进行繁育、授精或孵化的
senses.example: Artificial insemination has become routine in dairy farming.
senses.exampleCN: 人工授精在奶牛养殖中已很常规。
senses.why: Artificial insemination is dated 1894. The phrase names the exact point where a human procedure replaces a natural act, and the adjective then spreads to incubation and breeding.
senses.whyCN: artificial insemination 记录于 1894 年。这个短语点出了人的程序替代自然行为的那一步，形容词随后扩散到孵化与育种。

senses.title: Added in the factory
senses.titleCN: 人工添加的：配方里那几勺不是地里长的
senses.definition: of flavours, colours or additives in food, made industrially rather than obtained naturally
senses.definitionCN: 食品中的香料、色素或添加剂，由工业制成而非取自天然
senses.example: The drink contains artificial sweeteners and no fruit juice.
senses.exampleCN: 这种饮料含人工甜味剂，没有果汁。
senses.why: Industrial food makes the contrast sharp: a flavour can be synthesized in a plant. The adjective marks the origin of the ingredient, not its taste.
senses.whyCN: 工业食品让对比变得尖锐：一种味道可以在工厂里合成。这个形容词标记的是成分的来源，而不是它的味道。

senses.title: A line drawn by decision
senses.titleCN: 人为的、牵强的：自然界里找不到那条线
senses.definition: created by human convention or choice rather than by nature; contrived
senses.definitionCN: 由人的惯例或选择造成而非自然形成的；牵强的
senses.example: The border between the two dialects is artificial.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种方言之间的界线是人为划定的。
senses.why: A transferred 19th–20th century use: where nature shows a continuum, people draw a line. What is drawn rather than found is artificial, hence 'contrived'.
senses.whyCN: 这是 19–20 世纪的引申用法：自然呈现的是一条连续带，人却画了一条线。被画出来而不是被发现的，就是 artificial，因而有“牵强”之义。

senses.title: A person made by law
senses.titleCN: 法律拟制的：法律把一个组织当作人
senses.definition: (law) created by legal fiction, as an artificial person, a corporation
senses.definitionCN: （法律）依法律拟制而成立的，如法人
senses.example: A company is an artificial person and cannot be imprisoned.
senses.exampleCN: 公司是法人，不能被监禁。
senses.why: Legal language calls a corporation a person by convention. The entity has no body; its personality is made by rule, which is precisely the old sense 'made by art'.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言按惯例把公司称作人。这个实体没有身体，它的人格由规则做成，正是古老的“由技艺做成”之义。

senses.title: The day as people count it
senses.titleCN: 人为的一日：从日出到日落的那一段
senses.definition: (historical, of a day) measured from sunrise to sunset, as opposed to the natural 24-hour day
senses.definitionCN: （历史用法）按日出到日落计的一日，与自然的二十四小时日相对
senses.example: In old almanacs the artificial day was divided into twelve unequal hours.
senses.exampleCN: 旧历书中，人为的一日被分成十二个长短不等的时辰。
senses.why: This is the earliest English use, late 14c.: artificial day against natural day. The span is fixed by human reckoning of sunrise and sunset, so it is artificial in the original sense of 'by art'.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语最早的用法，14 世纪末：artificial day 对 natural day。这一段由人对日出日落的计算来定，所以是“由技艺”意义上的 artificial。

intro.en: Artificial begins as a Latin phrase for 'belonging to skill': ars plus facere, art plus making. English borrows it to mean 'not natural', and then lets it slide from materials to statements, manners and finally legal persons.
intro.cn: artificial 起初是拉丁语里“属于技艺”的说法：ars 加 facere，技艺加制作。英语借来表示“非自然”，随后让它从材料滑向陈述、举止，最后滑向法律上的人。

items.en: The root *ar- 'to fit together' is the reconstructed source of Latin ars 'skill, craft'. There is no written PIE evidence, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *ar-“拼合、使相合”是拉丁 ars“技艺、手艺”的重构来源。没有 PIE 书面证据，这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Latin ars (stem art-) 'skill, craft' plus -fex from facere 'to do, make' gives artifex 'craftsman, master of an art'. Its derivative artificium means 'a work of art, skill, a system'.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars（词干 art-）“技艺、手艺”加 -fex（来自 facere“做、造”）构成 artifex“工匠、技艺大师”。其派生词 artificium 义为“技艺之作、技艺、体系”。

items.en: Artificialis 'of or belonging to art' passes into Old French as artificial, still a neutral word about craft. English takes it in the late 14c. as 'not natural or spontaneous'.
items.cn: artificialis“属于技艺的”进入古法语作 artificial，仍是一个关于手艺的中性词。英语于 14 世纪末借入，义为“非自然的、非自发的”。

items.en: The earliest English use is the phrase artificial day, the span from sunrise to sunset as opposed to the natural 24-hour day. 'Made by man, contrived by human skill and labour' is recorded from the early 15c.
items.cn: 英语最早用法是 artificial day，即从日出到日落的一段，与自然的二十四小时日相对。“由人制造、靠人的技艺与劳动做成”记录于 15 世纪初。

items.en: From the 16c. the word attaches to anything made in imitation of, or as a substitute for, the natural — light, tears, teeth, flowers. 'Fictitious, assumed, not genuine' is from the 1640s, 'insincere, full of affectation' from the 1590s.
items.cn: 自 16 世纪起，这个词附着于一切模仿自然或替代自然之物——光、眼泪、牙齿、花。“虚构的、假定的、不真实的”始于 17 世纪 40 年代，“不真诚、充满做作”始于 16 世纪 90 年代。

items.en: Artificial insemination dates from 1894; artificial intelligence was coined in 1956. The modern word now covers food additives, medical replacement and legal persons without leaving its first sense of 'made by skill'.
items.cn: 人工授精始于 1894 年；人工智能于 1956 年被造出。现代这个词覆盖食品添加剂、医学替代物与法人，却始终没有离开最初“由技艺做成”的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the ars or fac- root but not the same history: artifice and artisan are kin, artful is a false friend in meaning, factitious comes through another Latin branch. The second group offers true synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ars 或 fac- 词根，但历史并不相同：artifice 与 artisan 是同族，artful 在词义上是假朋友，factitious 走的是另一条拉丁分支。第二组才是真正的近义词。

entries.definition: a clever device or trick. It is the noun inside artificial: artifex, the maker, plus -ium.
entries.definitionCN: 巧计；诡计。它就是 artificial 里的那个名词：artifex“工匠”加 -ium。

entries.definition: skilful, often cunningly so. It is art plus -ful, and never passed through artificialis, so it does not mean unnatural.
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙的，常指狡黠。它是 art 加 -ful，从未经过 artificialis，所以并不表示“不自然”。

entries.definition: a skilled craftsman. From Italian artigiano, from Latin artitus, 'instructed in arts'.
entries.definitionCN: 工匠。来自意大利语 artigiano，上溯拉丁 artitus“受过技艺训练”。

entries.definition: manufactured, artificial, not natural. From Latin facticius 'made by art', from facere 'to make'; it is a cousin, not the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 人造的、非自然的。来自拉丁 facticius“由技艺做成”，源自 facere“做”；它是表亲，不是同一个词。

entries.definition: produced by chemical synthesis rather than found in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 化学合成的，而非天然存在的。

entries.definition: made by people rather than by natural processes; the everyday twin of artificial.
entries.definitionCN: 人造的；artificial 的日常同义词。

entries.definition: not genuine, made to look real in order to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 假的；为骗人而做得像真的。

entries.definition: imitated or reproduced for display or testing, as simulated leather.
entries.definitionCN: 为展示或测试而仿制的，如仿皮。

entries.definition: deliberately arranged and therefore unnatural or forced.
entries.definitionCN: 刻意安排的，因而显得不自然、勉强。

normalIntro.en: The word is a workshop in miniature: ars is the skill, -fic- is the making, -al only makes it an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一座缩小的作坊：ars 是技艺，-fic- 是制作，-al 只是把它变成形容词。

normal.en: artificial = arti (ars, skill) + fici (facere, make) + -al: 'made by skill'.
normal.cn: artificial = arti（ars，技艺）+ fici（facere，做）+ -al：由技艺做成。

normal.en: -fic- is the same 'make' as in factory and manufacture; artificial things are made in a workshop, not grown in a field.
normal.cn: -fic- 与 factory、manufacture 里那个“做”相同；人造之物诞生在作坊，不长在田里。

normal.en: artful is not artificial: artful means skilful or cunning, while artificial means not natural.
normal.cn: artful 不是 artificial：artful 是巧妙或狡黠，artificial 是不自然。

normal.en: Artificial light, artificial flavour, artificial smile: one word marks three replacements.
normal.cn: 人工光、人工香料、做作的笑：同一个词标记了三处替代。

normal.en: A corporation is an artificial person: a person made of paper, not of birth.
normal.cn: 公司是 artificial person：一个由纸做成、而非由出生而来的人。

abstract.en: Nature grows; art makes. The suffix -al only turns the workshop into an adjective.
abstract.cn: 自然负责生长，技艺负责制造；-al 只是把作坊变成形容词。

abstract.en: Every artificial thing is a claim about the real thing it stands in for.
abstract.cn: 每一件人造之物，都是关于它所替代的那件真东西的一项主张。

abstract.en: The word moves from materials to manners: once a thing can be made, a smile can be made too.
abstract.cn: 这个词从材料走到举止：既然东西能造，笑容也能造。

examples.en: The lake is artificial, fed by a canal from the river.
examples.cn: 这个湖是人工的，由一条引自河里的渠道供水。

examples.en: Her artificial cheerfulness disappeared the moment the guests left.
examples.cn: 客人一走，她那做出来的高兴劲儿就消失了。

examples.en: Artificial intelligence can now draft a contract but cannot sign one.
examples.cn: 人工智能如今能起草合同，却不能签字。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: arti（技艺）+ fici（做）+ al——用技艺做出来的，不是自然长出来的，就是“人造的”；做得像真的，就成了“假的、做作的”。

root: 源自拉丁 artificialis ← artificium“技艺之作” ← artifex“工匠”（ars“技艺”+ -fex ← facere“做”）+ -al；字面义“由技艺做成”，故引申为“人造的、非自然的、假装的”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses follow one line: what is made instead of grown, then what is made instead of supplied by nature, then what is made to look true, then what is made to look felt, and at the end what is made by law alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项沿一条线走：不是长成而是做成，不是自然供给而是技术供给，做成像真的，做成像有感情的，最后是只由法律做成的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an orchid in a glass case, fed, lit and propped up by human skill.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃罩里的兰花，由人的技艺喂养、照明、支撑。

branches.en: MADE VS SUPPLIED: objects manufactured, and natural processes replaced by technique.
branches.cn: 造出来的与供给的：制造的物品，以及被技术替代的自然过程。

branches.en: SUBSTITUTES AND ADDITIVES: the artificial tooth or flower, and the factory flavour.
branches.cn: 替代品与添加剂：假牙假花，以及工厂里的香料。

branches.en: INVENTED AND CONTRIVED: a fabricated account, and a border drawn where nature shows a continuum.
branches.cn: 编造与牵强：编出来的说法，以及在连续带上画出的界线。

branches.en: MANUFACTURED MANNER: a made smile, and a day counted from sunrise to sunset by human reckoning.
branches.cn: 做出来的样子：造出的笑容，以及按人的计算从日出到日落的一日。

branches.en: TECHNIQUE IN BODY AND LAW: breeding by procedure, and the corporation made a person by rule.
branches.cn: 身体与法律中的技术：以程序繁育，以及按规则被做成人的公司。

intro.en: Artificial is a Latin compound wearing two suffixes: the root ars supplies art-, facere supplies -fic-, and -al turns the whole into an adjective. Its family spreads through -ly, -ity and the Latin nouns artifex and artificium.
intro.cn: artificial 是一个戴了两层后缀的拉丁复合词：词根 ars 提供 art-，facere 提供 -fic-，-al 把整体变成形容词。它的词族再经 -ly、-ity 以及拉丁名词 artifex、artificium 扩散。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both halves: ars 'skill' and facere 'to make', joined in artifex and artificium, then adjectivized as artificialis. The English -al, -ity and -ly came through French and Latin channels.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都由拉丁语提供：ars“技艺”与 facere“做”，在 artifex 与 artificium 中结合，再加 -alis 成为形容词。英语的 -al、-ity、-ly 经法语与拉丁语渠道而来。

items.meaning: made by skill, not by nature
items.meaningCN: 由技艺做成而非自然的
items.example: The artificial flowers looked almost real.
items.exampleCN: 这些假花几乎像真的一样。

items.meaning: by human technique
items.example: The fruit was artificially ripened.
items.exampleCN: 这水果是人工催熟的。

items.meaning: the quality of being made or fake
items.example: The artificiality of the scene was obvious.
items.exampleCN: 那个场景的虚假显而易见。

items.meaning: a made device; a trick
items.example: He won by artifice rather than skill.
items.exampleCN: 他靠诡计而非真本事取胜。

items.meaning: a maker or inventor
items.example: The artificer repaired the clockwork.
items.exampleCN: 制作者修好了这套钟表机械。

items.meaning: craftsman, master of an art
items.example: The word artifex named the maker, not the thing made.
items.exampleCN: artifex 这个词命名的是制作者，不是制成品。

items.meaning: made, not natural; artificial
items.example: The factitious enthusiasm fooled no one.
items.exampleCN: 那份装出来的热情骗不了人。

items.meaning: to make by hand or machine
items.example: The factory manufactures glass lenses.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂制造玻璃镜片。

items.meaning: something made by human skill
items.example: The dig produced artifacts from three centuries.
items.exampleCN: 这次发掘出土了三个世纪的器物。

definition_zh: 人工地；人为地；不自然地；虚假地；牵强地；靠机器维持地
definition_en: in a way produced by human skill or contrivance rather than by nature, and hence often in a way that is not genuine, not spontaneous, or not natural
core_image: 一只机械蜂停在真花上，花蜜是糖水调的，温度是旋钮定的——每一处本该由自然决定的地方，都换成了人的手
scene: The lab director waves at the tank and says: The reef is artificially lit, so the coral can grow where sunlight never reaches.
sceneCN: 这里 artificially 是「人工地」（第 1 个义项：以人工技术而非自然过程产生的方式）；句意：这块礁石用人工光照，好让珊瑚在阳光照不到的地方生长。画面里有水槽、灯排和温度旋钮。

pos.zh: 人工地；人为地；不自然地；虚假地；牵强地

collocations.zh: 人工制造的；人为造成的

derivatives.zh: 人造的；人工的；虚假的；做作的

senses.title: By human technique
senses.titleCN: 人工地：用技术替自然做那一步
senses.definition: in a way that is produced by human technique rather than by a natural process
senses.definitionCN: 以人工技术而非自然过程产生的方式
senses.example: The pond is artificially aerated to keep the fish alive.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼塘靠人工增氧让鱼活下来。
senses.why: The adverb is recorded in the early 15c. as 'by art or human skill and contrivance'. The suffix -ly adds manner to artificial: the question is not what a thing is, but whose agency produced it.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词记录于 15 世纪初，义为“靠技艺或人的技能与设计”。后缀 -ly 给 artificial 加上“方式”：问题不在于东西是什么，而在于它是谁做出来的。

senses.title: Because someone decided so
senses.titleCN: 人为地：不是自然发生，而是被决定成这样
senses.definition: as a result of human decision or intervention rather than natural causes
senses.definitionCN: 由人的决定或干预而非自然原因造成
senses.example: Rents were kept artificially low by subsidies.
senses.exampleCN: 补贴把租金人为地压得很低。
senses.why: Once 'by human skill' is transferred from objects to outcomes, the adverb names a cause. A price is artificially low when a decision, not the market, holds it down.
senses.whyCN: 一旦“靠人的技艺”从物品转到结果上，这个副词就指向一个原因。价格之所以是 artificially low，是因为压住它的是决定，而不是市场。

senses.title: With a manufactured manner
senses.titleCN: 不自然地：表情和语气是摆出来的
senses.definition: in an insincere or affected manner; without spontaneity
senses.definitionCN: 以不真诚或做作的方式；缺乏自然流露
senses.example: She smiled artificially and looked away.
senses.exampleCN: 她不自然地笑了笑，把目光移开。
senses.why: The 1590s adjective sense 'full of affectation' gives the adverb its social use. Behaviour that is made rather than felt is performed, and a performance can be seen.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 90 年代形容词“充满做作”的义项给了副词这层社交用法。做出来而非感受出来的举止是一种表演，而表演是看得出来的。

senses.title: In a way that is not true
senses.titleCN: 虚假地：把做出来的东西当成真的
senses.definition: falsely; in a way that is not genuine
senses.definitionCN: 虚假地；以不真实的方式
senses.example: The boom was artificially sustained by cheap credit.
senses.exampleCN: 那场繁荣是靠廉价信贷虚假地维持的。
senses.why: From the 1640s 'fictitious, assumed' sense: what has a maker can be presented as having none. The adverb marks the pretence, not the material.
senses.whyCN: 这来自 17 世纪 40 年代“虚构的、假定的”义：有制造者的东西可以被说成没有制造者。副词标记的是这层伪装，而不是材料。

senses.title: Under controlled conditions
senses.titleCN: 在人工条件下：把野外搬进实验室
senses.definition: under laboratory or otherwise controlled conditions rather than in the wild
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室或其他受控条件下，而非在自然环境中
senses.example: The crystals were grown artificially at high pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这些晶体是在高压下人工培育的。
senses.why: Modern science makes 'by human skill' literal: temperature, pressure and light are set by instruments. What happens there would not happen in nature.
senses.whyCN: 现代科学让“靠人的技艺”变成字面意思：温度、压力、光照都由仪器设定。那里发生的事，在自然中不会发生。

senses.title: Sustained by a machine
senses.titleCN: 靠机器维持地：身体的那一步交给了设备
senses.definition: by mechanical means, as in artificially ventilated or artificially fed patients
senses.definitionCN: 以机械手段，如对病人进行人工通气或人工喂食
senses.example: He was artificially ventilated for three days after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故后他靠人工呼吸机维持了三天。
senses.why: Twentieth-century medicine extends the adverb to bodies: a machine performs what an organ cannot. The word keeps its old meaning of agency — the breath is made, not given.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的医学把这个副词扩展到身体：机器替器官完成它做不到的事。词仍保留“谁在做”的旧义——这口气是造出来的，不是被给予的。

senses.title: By a line drawn, not found
senses.titleCN: 牵强地、人为划分地：自然界没有那条线
senses.definition: by an artificial distinction; in a contrived or arbitrary way
senses.definitionCN: 按人为的区分；以牵强或武断的方式
senses.example: The two subjects are artificially separated in the curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 这两门学科在课程里被牵强地分开了。
senses.why: Where nature shows a continuum, institutions draw boundaries. The adverb of the 'contrived' sense marks a division that exists because it was declared, not because it was found.
senses.whyCN: 自然呈现连续带的地方，制度画出边界。“牵强”义的这个副词，标记的是一种因为被宣布、而非因为被发现才存在的划分。

senses.title: In a constructed scenario
senses.titleCN: 人为设定地：情境本身是搭出来的
senses.definition: in a situation that has been deliberately constructed for study or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在为研究或论证刻意构造的情境中
senses.example: The model was tested on artificially generated data.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在人工生成的数据上做了测试。
senses.why: Research usage: data or scenarios are produced rather than observed. This is the 20th-century descendant of 'contrived', applied to the conditions of an experiment rather than to a border.
senses.whyCN: 这是研究用法：数据或情境是被生产出来的，不是被观察到的。它是“牵强”义在 20 世纪的后代，只是用在实验条件上，而不是用在边界上。

intro.en: Artificially is the adjective artificial plus the adverb suffix -ly, a formation already present in the early 15c. It is not artfully: that word comes from artful, means 'skilfully or cunningly', and never passed through Latin artificialis.
intro.cn: artificially 是形容词 artificial 加副词后缀 -ly，这种构词在 15 世纪初已经存在。它不是 artfully：后者来自 artful，义为“巧妙地或狡黠地”，从未经过拉丁 artificialis。

items.en: Latin ars 'skill' is reconstructed to the root *ar- 'to fit together'. There is no written PIE record, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars“技艺”被重构到词根 *ar-“拼合”。没有 PIE 书面记录，这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: ars (stem art-) plus -fex from facere 'to make' gives artifex 'craftsman'; artificium 'skill, a work of art'; artificialis 'of or belonging to art'.
items.cn: ars（词干 art-）加 -fex（来自 facere“做”）构成 artifex“工匠”；artificium“技艺、技艺之作”；artificialis“属于技艺的”。

items.en: Old French artificial carries the Latin adjective into English, where it first means 'not natural or spontaneous'. The adverb is built on this English adjective, not borrowed whole.
items.cn: 古法语 artificial 把这个拉丁形容词带进英语，最初义为“非自然的、非自发的”。副词是在这个英语形容词上构成的，不是整体借来的。

items.en: Artificially is recorded as 'by art or human skill and contrivance', formed with -ly (2), the adverbial suffix from Old English -lice and Proto-Germanic *-liko-, cognate with like and lich.
items.cn: artificially 记录为“靠技艺或人的技能与设计”，由 -ly（第 2 类）构成；这个副词后缀来自古英语 -lice、原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与 like、lich 同源。

items.en: As the adjective gains 'imitation', 'fictitious' and 'insincere', the adverb follows: artificially lit, artificially shed tears, artificially cheerful. The manner sense and the material sense run in parallel.
items.cn: 随着形容词获得“模仿”“虚构”“不真诚”等义，副词也跟着走：人工照明、假意落泪、装出高兴。方式义与材料义并行。

items.en: Technical and medical uses widen the adverb: artificially inseminated (1894 onward), artificially ventilated, artificially generated data. Artfully remains a different word, sharing only the Latin ars behind art.
items.cn: 技术与医学用法拓宽了这个副词：人工授精（1894 年起）、人工通气、人工生成的数据。artfully 仍是另一个词，只共享 art 背后的拉丁 ars。

note.en: The look-alike group is dangerous because artfully sounds like a close relative but means 'skilfully, cunningly'. The near-meaning group shares the idea of something not produced by nature.
note.cn: 形近组之所以危险，是因为 artfully 听起来像近亲，意思却是“巧妙地、狡黠地”。近义组共享“不是自然产生”这一观念。

entries.definition: skilfully, often with cunning. Built on artful (art + -ful), it never means 'by artificial means'.
entries.definitionCN: 巧妙地，常含狡黠。它由 artful（art + -ful）构成，从不表示“用人工手段”。

entries.definition: made by human skill rather than nature; the base of the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 人造的；人工的。副词的原形。

entries.definition: the state of being artificial; the -ity noun that replaces -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 人造性；虚假。把 -ly 换成 -ity 得到的名词。

entries.definition: in a manufactured or artificial way. From factitious, another branch of the 'make' root.
entries.definitionCN: 以人造或做作的方式。来自 factitious，是“做”这个词根的另一分支。

entries.definition: in a way that departs from what is normal in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 不自然地；违背自然常态地。

entries.definition: by chemical synthesis rather than by natural production.
entries.definitionCN: 以化学合成方式，而非自然生成。

entries.definition: in a way that is not true or not genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 虚假地；不真实地。

entries.definition: without genuine feeling; in an affected way.
entries.definitionCN: 不真诚地；做作地。

entries.definition: in a deliberately arranged and therefore forced way.
entries.definitionCN: 以刻意安排因而显得勉强的方式。

normalIntro.en: Artificially is the adverb of agency: it answers 'by whose doing?' rather than 'what is it?'.
normalIntro.cn: artificially 是回答“谁做的”的副词：它答的是“由谁动手”，而不是“它是什么”。

normal.en: artificial + ly: add -ly and the adjective becomes the manner of making.
normal.cn: artificial + ly：加上 -ly，形容词就变成了“制作的方式”。

normal.en: artificially is not artfully: one means 'by technique', the other 'skilfully'.
normal.cn: artificially 不是 artfully：前者是“用技术”，后者是“巧妙地”。

normal.en: Artificially sweetened, artificially lit, artificially low: each adverb names the hand behind the result.
normal.cn: 人工加甜、人工照明、人为压低：每个副词都点出结果背后的那只手。

normal.en: In a hospital, artificially ventilated means a machine is doing the breathing.
normal.cn: 在医院里，artificially ventilated 意味着机器在做呼吸这件事。

normal.en: In research, artificially generated data has a maker, not a source.
normal.cn: 在研究里，人工生成的数据有一个制造者，而不是一个来源。

abstract.en: The adverb turns nature into a background and a technique into the subject.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把自然降为背景，把技术抬成主语。

abstract.en: Every artificially produced thing is also a claim about what would have happened without the hand.
abstract.cn: 每一件人工产物，也是关于“若没有这只手会怎样”的一项主张。

abstract.en: From light to breath to data, the same word marks the point where a human procedure takes over.
abstract.cn: 从光到呼吸再到数据，同一个词标记出人的程序接管的那一点。

examples.en: The juice is artificially sweetened, with no sugar at all.
examples.cn: 这种果汁是人工加甜的，完全不含糖。

examples.en: Critics say the shortage was artificially created to raise prices.
examples.cn: 批评者说这场短缺是为抬高价格而人为制造的。

examples.en: The samples were artificially aged to test the coating.
examples.cn: 这些样品被人工老化，以检验涂层。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: artificial（人造的）+ ly（……地）——用技艺做出来的那种方式，就是“人工地”；做给人看的样子，就是“不自然地”。

root: = artificial + -ly；artificial 源自拉丁 artificialis ← artificium ← artifex（ars“技艺”+ -fex ← facere“做”）+ -al。副词后缀 -ly 来自古英语 -lice、原始日耳曼语 *-liko-，与 like 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one question: who or what produced this? The answer can be a technique, a decision, a performance, a pretence, a machine, a drawn line, or a constructed scenario.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个问题：这是谁、用什么造出来的？答案可以是技术、决定、表演、伪装、机器、画出的界线，或搭出的情境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mechanical bee on a real flower, with syrup for nectar and a dial for warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只机械蜂停在真花上，花蜜是糖水，温度靠旋钮。

branches.en: TECHNIQUE AND LAB CONDITIONS: made by human skill, and made under settings that nature would not supply.
branches.cn: 技术与实验条件：靠人的技艺做成，以及在自然不会给出的设定下做成。

branches.en: DECISION AND CONSTRUCTION: an outcome held in place by policy, and a scenario built for study.
branches.cn: 决定与构造：由政策维持的结果，以及为研究搭出的情境。

branches.en: MANNER AND PRETENCE: a performed smile, and a false picture presented as fact.
branches.cn: 举止与伪装：表演出来的笑容，以及被当作事实呈现的假象。

branches.en: THE MACHINE IN THE BODY: breath and feeding carried out by equipment.
branches.cn: 身体里的机器：由设备完成呼吸与进食。

branches.en: THE DRAWN LINE: a division that exists because it was declared.
branches.cn: 画出的界线：因为被宣布才存在的划分。

intro.en: Artificially is a three-layer word: a Latin root compound (ars + facere), a Latin adjective suffix -al, and a Germanic adverb suffix -ly. Learning to peel the layers explains both its meaning and its false friend artfully.
intro.cn: artificially 有三层：拉丁词根复合（ars + facere）、拉丁形容词后缀 -al、日耳曼副词后缀 -ly。学会逐层剥开，既能解释它的意思，也能解释假朋友 artfully。

latinIntro.en: The Latin part stops at -al: artificialis. The -ly is not Latin at all — it is Old English -lice, cognate with like, which is why the adverb looks so different from Latin adverbs in -e or -iter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁部分到 -al 为止：artificialis。-ly 完全不是拉丁的——它是古英语 -lice，与 like 同源，所以这个副词看起来和以 -e、-iter 结尾的拉丁副词很不一样。

items.meaning: by human technique or contrivance
items.example: The lake is artificially stocked with trout.
items.exampleCN: 湖里是人工放养的鳟鱼。

items.meaning: made rather than natural
items.example: The teeth are artificial but the smile is real.
items.exampleCN: 牙是假的，笑是真的。

items.meaning: the quality of being made or feigned
items.example: The artificiality of the lighting ruined the mood.
items.exampleCN: 人造的灯光破坏了气氛。

items.meaning: a made device; cunning
items.example: No artifice could hide the missing page.
items.exampleCN: 再巧的手段也藏不住缺页。

items.meaning: maker, craftsman
items.example: The artificer built the model from brass.
items.exampleCN: 工匠用黄铜做出了这个模型。

items.meaning: skilful, often cunning — not 'artificial'
items.meaningCN: 巧妙的，常含狡黠——不是“人造的”
items.example: She made an artful exit before the argument began.
items.exampleCN: 争吵开始前她巧妙地退场了。

items.meaning: manufactured, not natural
items.example: The calm was factitious, not real.
items.exampleCN: 那份平静是装出来的，不是真的。

items.meaning: put together by chemistry
items.example: The fabric is synthetic but feels soft.
items.exampleCN: 这块布料是合成的，但手感柔软。

items.meaning: to make, especially in quantity
items.example: They manufacture the devices in one plant.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一家工厂里制造这些设备。

definition_zh: 查明；弄清；探明；核实；确定；确信；（古）告知；确保
definition_en: to find out something with certainty, to establish a fact or figure by investigation or measurement, and formerly to assure or inform someone
core_image: 桌上摊着一张写满传言的纸，有人提灯逐条划掉，直到只剩一行能被证实的字——那行字就是被“弄确定”的东西
scene: The inspector says: We must ascertain who was in the building before the fire began.
sceneCN: 这里 ascertain 是「查明」（第 1 个义项：通过询问、核对或调查发现事实）；句意：我们必须查明起火之前谁在楼里。画面里有提灯、值班簿和一张划满线的纸。

pos.zh: 查明；弄清；探明；核实；确定

senses.title: Find out a fact
senses.titleCN: 查明：把传言问到只剩事实
senses.definition: to discover a fact or the truth by asking, checking or investigating
senses.definitionCN: 通过询问、核对或调查发现事实或真相
senses.example: The police are trying to ascertain how the door was opened.
senses.exampleCN: 警方正试图查明门是怎么被打开的。
senses.why: The modern sense 'find out for sure by experiment or investigation' is recorded by 1794, but the word began in the 15c. as 'to make certain'. Investigation is the method by which a matter is brought into certainty.
senses.whyCN: 现代义“通过实验或调查确实查明”记录于 1794 年，但这个词在 15 世纪原义是“使确定”。调查就是把一件事带到“确定”状态的方法。

senses.title: Fix a figure by measuring
senses.titleCN: 探明、测知：把不确定的量量成一个数
senses.definition: to establish a quantity, position or property by measurement or test
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量或检验确定数量、位置或性质
senses.example: Engineers ascertained the load the bridge could bear.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师探明了这座桥能承受的荷载。
senses.why: Latin certus means 'fixed, settled'. Measuring is literally fixing: before the test the load is unknown, after it the figure is settled and can be quoted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 certus 义为“固定的、已定的”。测量就是字面上的“固定”：测试前荷载未知，测试后这个数被定下来，可以直接引用。

senses.title: Check a claim
senses.titleCN: 核实：把一句话拿去对证
senses.definition: to verify that a statement or report is true
senses.definitionCN: 核实某陈述或报告是否属实
senses.example: The editor could not ascertain whether the letter was genuine.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑无法核实这封信是否真实。
senses.why: The prefix a- (ad-, 'to') plus certain means 'bring to a sure state'. A claim is checked by being brought up against evidence until doubt is removed.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a-（ad-，“向”）加 certain 义为“带到确定状态”。一句话被拿去与证据对照，直到疑点被去掉，才算核实。

senses.title: Reach a settled judgement
senses.titleCN: 断定：筛到最后，只剩一个结论
senses.definition: to determine something and come to be sure of it
senses.definitionCN: 确定某事并最终对其确信
senses.example: From the records we ascertained that the meeting had never taken place.
senses.exampleCN: 从记录看，我们断定那场会议从未举行。
senses.why: Latin certus came from cernere, 'to sift, separate, decide'. Ascertaining is a sifting: alternatives are removed until one remains, and the judgement inherits the sieve.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 certus 出自 cernere“筛、分开、判定”。ascertain 就是一次筛选：把其他可能一一去掉，直到只剩一个；判断继承了这把筛子。

senses.title: Pin down a person or thing
senses.titleCN: 查明（身份、下落）：把人或物定位到一个确定点
senses.definition: to find out who or where someone or something is
senses.definitionCN: 查明某人是谁或某物在哪里
senses.example: They ascertained the identity of the woman from a single photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 他们凭一张照片查明了那名女子的身份。
senses.why: The same act applied to a target: an unknown person is located and named. The 'fixed' quality of certus is what a name supplies — the person stops being an anonymous possibility.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动作用在目标上：一个未知的人被定位、被命名。certus 的“固定”正是名字所提供的东西——那个人不再是一个匿名的可能性。

senses.title: Settle a value or standard
senses.titleCN: 确定（数值、标准）：让它从此不再变
senses.definition: to establish a value or standard definitively
senses.definitionCN: 确定性地确立某一数值或标准
senses.example: The committee ascertained the minimum wage for the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会确定了来年的最低工资。
senses.why: Here the verb creates certainty rather than finding it: a decision fixes a standard. English uses ascertain in this legislative sense because the outcome is a settled figure.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词是在制造确定，而不是在发现确定：决定把一个标准固定下来。英语在这个立法意义上用 ascertain，因为结果是一个被定下的数。

senses.title: Make sure
senses.titleCN: 使确定、确保：古一点的“让某事成为定局”
senses.definition: (formal, older use) to make certain or ensure something
senses.definitionCN: （正式或较早用法）使某事确定或有保证
senses.example: The treaty was signed to ascertain the border between the two states.
senses.exampleCN: 条约的签署是为了确保两国之间的边界。
senses.why: This is the verb's oldest English layer, 'to make certain'. The modern 'find out' is a specialization: one way of making a thing certain is to establish it.
senses.whyCN: 这是动词最早的英语层次——“使确定”。现代的“查明”是一个专门化：让一件事确定的方式之一，就是把它确立起来。

senses.title: Tell someone for sure
senses.titleCN: （古）告知、保证：让对方心里有底
senses.definition: (obsolete) to inform someone or give them assurance
senses.definitionCN: （已废）告知某人或向其作出保证
senses.example: He ascertained them that the ship had arrived safely.
senses.exampleCN: 他向他们保证船已平安抵达。
senses.why: Early 15c. ascertain meant 'to inform, to give assurance', from Old French acertener 'to assure, certify'. The speaker makes the hearer certain; this sense is now obsolete and survives only in dictionaries.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪初 ascertain 义为“告知、给予保证”，来自古法语 acertener“使确信、证明”。说话人让听者确定；这个义项现已废弃，只留在词典里。

intro.en: Ascertain begins as a French verb meaning 'to make sure', built from a- 'to' and certain, whose Latin base certus is literally 'sifted, decided'. English first used it for reassuring people, then narrowed it to finding facts out.
intro.cn: ascertain 起初是一个法语动词，义为“使确定”，由 a-“向”与 certain 构成，后者拉丁词基 certus 字面是“筛过的、定了的”。英语先用它表示让人安心，后来窄化为查明事实。

items.en: The root *krei- 'to sieve' is the reconstructed source of Latin cernere 'to sift, separate, decide'. No written PIE record survives, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *krei-“筛”是拉丁 cernere“筛、分开、判定”的重构来源。没有 PIE 书面记录留存，这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Latin certus 'determined, resolved, fixed, settled', originally a variant past participle of cernere, also meant 'placed beyond doubt, proved'. Its sense of a sifted residue becoming a decision is the seed of the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁 certus“已定、已决、固定、确定”，原为 cernere 的变体过去分词，也义为“无可怀疑、已被证明”。筛剩下的东西成为决定，这一意象是整个词族的种子。

items.en: Vulgar Latin *certanus, an extended form of certus, gives Old French certain 'reliable, sure, assured'. The adjective is the base of the verb that follows.
items.cn: 俗拉丁 *certanus（certus 的扩展形式）给出古法语 certain“可靠的、确信的、有保证的”。这个形容词是随后动词的基础。

items.en: acertener 'to assure, certify' is formed with a- 'to' plus certain, literally 'to bring to a sure state'. Anglo-French acerteiner carries it across the Channel.
items.cn: acertener“使确信、证明”由 a-“向”加 certain 构成，字面即“带到确定状态”。英吉利法语 acerteiner 把它带过海峡。

items.en: Ascertain is recorded as 'to inform, to give assurance', a sense now obsolete. The speaker made the hearer certain rather than the speaker becoming certain himself.
items.cn: ascertain 记录为“告知、给予保证”，此义今已废弃。当时是说话人让听者确定，而不是说话人自己变得确定。

items.en: The meaning 'find out for sure by experiment or investigation' is attested by 1794, and ascertainable by 1765. The direction reverses: the mind now receives certainty from evidence rather than giving it to someone else.
items.cn: “通过实验或调查确实查明”义于 1794 年记录，ascertainable 于 1765 年出现。方向反了过来：心智现在从证据获得确定，而不是把确定给别人。

note.en: The first group is a trap: assert, ascetic and certain all sit near ascertain in spelling or sound, but only certain and certify share the cert- root. The second group gives the verbs that do the same work.
note.cn: 第一组是陷阱：assert、ascetic、certain 在拼写或读音上都靠近 ascertain，但只有 certain 与 certify 共享 cert- 词根。第二组才是做同一件事的动词。

entries.definition: to state firmly. From Latin asserere 'join to, claim', from serere 'join' — nothing to do with certus.
entries.definitionCN: 断言；坚称。来自拉丁 asserere“连接到、主张”，源自 serere“连接”，与 certus 无关。

entries.definition: practising severe self-discipline. From Greek askēsis 'exercise, training', not from Latin certus.
entries.definitionCN: 苦行的。来自希腊语 askēsis“锻炼、训练”，并非拉丁 certus。

entries.definition: sure, fixed; the adjective from which ascertain was built.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；certain 正是构成 ascertain 的那个形容词。

entries.definition: to confirm formally in writing. Built on cert- plus -ify, it shares the 'made sure' core.
entries.definitionCN: 证明；核证。由 cert- 加 -ify 构成，共享“使确定”的核心。

entries.definition: to find out or decide something firmly, from Latin determinare 'set bounds to'.
entries.definitionCN: 确定；查明。来自拉丁 determinare“划定界限”。

entries.definition: to establish that something is true or accurate.
entries.definitionCN: 核实；证实某事真实或准确。

entries.definition: to establish the truth of something already believed or reported.
entries.definitionCN: 确认；证实已相信或已报告之事。

entries.definition: to prove or show something to be true beyond doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 确立；证实某事无可怀疑。

entries.definition: to find something previously unknown, often by chance or search.
entries.definitionCN: 发现；找到原先未知之物，常靠搜寻或偶然。

normalIntro.en: The word is a- plus certain: to ascertain is to bring something to the state of being certain. The sifting image of cernere sits inside certus.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 a- 加 certain：ascertain 就是把某物带到“确定”的状态。certus 里藏着 cernere 那把筛子。

normal.en: a- (to) + certain: to ascertain is to bring a matter to certainty.
normal.cn: a-（向）+ certain：ascertain 就是把一件事带到确定。

normal.en: cert- comes from cernere, 'to sift': what is ascertained is what remains after doubt is sifted away.
normal.cn: cert- 出自 cernere“筛”：被 ascertain 的，是疑点被筛掉后剩下的东西。

normal.en: ascertain is not assert: assert claims, ascertain checks.
normal.cn: ascertain 不是 assert：assert 是声称，ascertain 是核对。

normal.en: A surveyor ascertains a height; a court ascertains damages; both fix a figure.
normal.cn: 测量员 ascertain 高度，法庭 ascertain 损害赔偿；两者都是把一个数定下来。

normal.en: The old sense was 'to assure someone'; the modern one is 'to become sure yourself'.
normal.cn: 旧义是“向别人保证”，今义是“自己变得确定”。

abstract.en: Certainty is a residue: sift the claims and the fact is what is left.
abstract.cn: 确定是一种剩余物：把各种说法筛掉，剩下的事实才是确定的。

abstract.en: Measurement is decision with an instrument: the unknown becomes a quoted number.
abstract.cn: 测量是借助仪器的决定：未知之物变成一个可以被引用的数。

abstract.en: The word reverses direction over six centuries: from giving certainty to receiving it from evidence.
abstract.cn: 六个世纪里这个词换了方向：从把确定给别人，到从证据那里接受确定。

examples.en: Investigators are still trying to ascertain the cause of the fire.
examples.cn: 调查人员仍在努力查明火灾原因。

examples.en: Please ascertain whether the train leaves from platform three.
examples.cn: 请核实这趟列车是否从三号站台发车。

examples.en: The exact age of the rock was ascertained by radiocarbon dating.
examples.cn: 这块岩石的确切年龄是用放射性碳定年法测定的。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: a（向）+ certain（确定的）——把一件事带到“确定”的状态，就是“查明、弄清”；再往前一步，就是“使确定、确保”。

root: 源自古法语 acertener（a-“向”+ certain“确定的”）← 俗拉丁 *certanus ← 拉丁 certus“已定的、确定的”（原为 cernere“筛、分开、判定”的变体过去分词）；核心是“使确定、筛到只剩事实”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all circle one move: bringing something into a state of certainty. Sometimes that means sifting evidence, sometimes measuring a figure, sometimes naming a person, sometimes simply telling someone so.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项绕着同一个动作转：把某物带进“确定”的状态。有时是筛证据，有时是量出一个数，有时是点出一个人的名字，有时只是告诉别人让他放心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp-lit table where claims are crossed out one by one until a single line remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下的一张桌子，说法被一条条划掉，只剩下一行。

branches.en: FINDING OUT: a fact sought by investigation, and a claim brought up against evidence.
branches.cn: 查明：以调查追出事实，以及把说法拿去与证据对证。

branches.en: FIXING A FIGURE: a quantity measured, and a standard settled by decision.
branches.cn: 定下一个数：被量出的量，以及由决定确立的标准。

branches.en: MAKING CERTAIN: a judgement reached by sifting, and the older sense of ensuring.
branches.cn: 使确定：筛出的判断，以及较早的“确保”义。

branches.en: PINNING A TARGET: an unknown person located and named.
branches.cn: 锁定目标：一个未知的人被定位并命名。

branches.en: THE OLD ASSURANCE: telling someone so that they may be certain.
branches.cn: 古老的保证：告诉别人，让他心里有底。

intro.en: Ascertain is a prefix plus an adjective turned verb: a- (from Latin ad-) plus certain. Its family grows with -able, -ment, -ty, -ly and the Latin cert- branch in certify and certificate.
intro.cn: ascertain 是前缀加“形容词转动词”：a-（来自拉丁 ad-）加 certain。词族再以 -able、-ment、-ty、-ly 生长，并在 certify、certificate 里延伸出拉丁 cert- 分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies certus and its source cernere 'to sift'. The a- is ad- reduced in French, and the -ain of certain is a French adjective ending, so the word reached English through French rather than directly from Rome.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 certus 及其来源 cernere“筛”。a- 是法语中弱化的 ad-，certain 的 -ain 是法语形容词词尾，所以这个词是经法语进入英语的，不是直接从罗马来。

items.meaning: to bring to certainty; to find out
items.example: They ascertained the cause within a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们一周内查明了原因。

items.meaning: fixed, sure, or some particular
items.example: One thing is certain: the door was unlocked.
items.exampleCN: 有一点是确定的：门没锁。

items.meaning: the state of being sure
items.example: We cannot speak with certainty about the motive.
items.exampleCN: 我们无法确定地说出动机。

items.meaning: surely, without doubt
items.example: The record certainly existed at some point.
items.exampleCN: 这份记录确实在某个时候存在过。

items.meaning: able to be found out
items.example: The cost is ascertainable from the invoices.
items.exampleCN: 费用可以从发票上查明。

items.meaning: the act of finding out
items.example: The ascertainment of the facts took months.
items.exampleCN: 事实的查明花了几个月。

items.meaning: to make certain in writing
items.example: A doctor certified the cause of death.
items.exampleCN: 一名医生证明了死因。

items.meaning: a document that makes something certain
items.example: She showed a certificate of ownership.
items.exampleCN: 她出示了所有权证书。

items.meaning: firm certainty of mind
items.example: He spoke with the certitude of a witness.
items.exampleCN: 他以证人的笃定口吻说话。

definition_zh: 评估；评价；估价；估值；税额核定；摊派额；（教育）测评；评估报告；损害赔偿评定
definition_en: the act of judging the value, quality or amount of something, the judgement or figure that results, and specifically the fixing of a tax, charge or loss
core_image: 一张旧木桌，估税员坐在纳税人对面，地契、收成账和税册摊开，笔尖在一栏里写下这块地今年该缴的数
scene: The teacher says: This assessment is about your essay, not about you.
sceneCN: 这里 assessment 是「教育测评」（第 4 个义项：测试并评判学生作业或进步的过程）；句意：这份测评评的是你的文章，不是你这个人。画面里有作文本、红笔和一张评分表。

pos.zh: 评估；评价；估价；税额核定；测评；评估报告

collocations.zh: 持续性测评；平时成绩评定

derivatives.zh: 评估员；估税员；理赔定损员
自我评估；自行申报纳税

senses.title: Judging quality or performance
senses.titleCN: 评估：把一件事的好坏量成判断
senses.definition: the act of judging the quality, importance or performance of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的质量、重要性或表现的行为
senses.example: The report offers a careful assessment of the risks.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对风险做了审慎的评估。
senses.why: The general 'estimation' sense is recorded from the 1620s, growing out of the tax sense: anything can be valued the way property is valued, by setting a figure on it.
senses.whyCN: 泛指的“估计”义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代，是从税务义长出来的：任何东西都能像财产那样被估值，方式是给它定一个数。

senses.title: Valuing property
senses.titleCN: 估价：给一块地、一栋房标个价
senses.definition: the act of estimating the value of property, especially for sale or taxation
senses.definitionCN: 估算财产价值的行为，尤指为出售或征税
senses.example: An assessment put the house at four hundred thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一次估价把这栋房子定为四十万英镑。
senses.why: The noun enters English in the 1530s as 'value of property for tax purposes'. A value must be fixed before a fraction of it can be demanded.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词于 16 世纪 30 年代进入英语，义为“供征税用的财产价值”。必须先定出一个价值，才能从其中抽取一份。

senses.title: Fixing the tax
senses.titleCN: 税额核定：官方替你算出该缴多少
senses.definition: the amount of tax or charge fixed by an authority, or the act of fixing it
senses.definitionCN: 官方确定的税额或费用，或确定该数额的行为
senses.example: The assessment on the land was raised after the new road was built.
senses.exampleCN: 新路建成后，这块地的税额被提高了。
senses.why: The 1540s sense is 'act of determining or adjusting a tax rate, charge or damages'. The official's sitting beside the taxpayer produced a definite sum, and the sum took the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 16 世纪 40 年代的义项是“确定或调整税率、费用或损害赔偿的行为”。官员坐在纳税人旁边，算出一个确定的数，这个数就继承了动作的名字。

senses.title: Testing a pupil
senses.titleCN: （教育）测评：把学习当成可估的东西来量
senses.definition: (education) the process of testing and judging a student's work or progress
senses.definitionCN: （教育）测试并评判学生作业或进步的过程
senses.example: Continuous assessment counts for forty percent of the final grade.
senses.exampleCN: 平时测评占最终成绩的百分之四十。
senses.why: This use is education jargon only from 1956, but its logic is old: a pupil's work is valued as property is valued, and the valuation is written down.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法 1956 年才成为教育行话，但其逻辑很老：学生的作业像财产一样被估值，而估值被写下来。

senses.title: Judging a patient
senses.titleCN: （医学）评估：先量清病情再决定
senses.definition: (medicine) the evaluation of a patient's condition or of a health risk
senses.definitionCN: （医学）对病人状况或健康风险的评估
senses.example: The nurse did a pain assessment before giving the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在给药前做了疼痛评估。
senses.why: Clinical use extends 'estimation' to the body: signs are collected and weighed. Nothing is priced, but everything is measured on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法把“估计”扩展到身体：体征被收集、被权衡。没有东西被标价，但一切都被放在量表上量过。

senses.title: The written judgement
senses.titleCN: 评估报告：落在纸上的那份判断
senses.definition: a report, statement or result that gives such a judgement
senses.definitionCN: 给出这种判断的报告、陈述或结果
senses.example: Her assessment was three pages long and ended with a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 她的评估报告有三页，结尾是一句警告。
senses.why: -ment makes nouns of result as well as act. Once the judging is done, the paper that carries the judgement is also an assessment.
senses.whyCN: -ment 既造“结果”名词，也造“动作”名词。评判做完之后，承载这个判断的那几页纸也叫 assessment。

senses.title: The insurer's figure
senses.titleCN: 保险定损：损失也要折成一个数
senses.definition: an estimate of the amount of loss or damage, as for an insurance claim
senses.definitionCN: 对损失或损坏金额的估算，如用于保险理赔
senses.example: The insurer's assessment came to less than the repair bill.
senses.exampleCN: 保险公司的定损额低于维修账单。
senses.why: Insurance inherits the tax structure: a loss is inspected, valued and fixed. The adjuster does what the tax assessor did — sits down, looks, and writes a sum.
senses.whyCN: 保险继承了税务的结构：损失被查看、估值、定数。理赔员做的事和估税员一样——坐下来，看一看，写下一个数。

senses.title: What you think of someone
senses.titleCN: 评价、看法：把一个人放在秤上
senses.definition: a judgement or opinion about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的判断或看法
senses.example: His assessment of the new manager was less harsh than mine.
senses.exampleCN: 他对新经理的评价没有我那么苛刻。
senses.why: The transferred sense 'to judge the value of a person or idea' is from 1934. Once people and ideas are valued, the resulting opinion is an assessment.
senses.whyCN: “评判一个人或一个想法的价值”这一引申义始于 1934 年。一旦人和想法被估值，得出的看法就是一项 assessment。

senses.title: A psychological measure
senses.titleCN: 心理评估：用一套量表读出状态
senses.definition: (psychology) a structured evaluation of a person's abilities, state or needs
senses.definitionCN: （心理学）对个人能力、状态或需求的结构化评估
senses.example: A psychological assessment was ordered before the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 审判前被要求做心理评估。
senses.why: Psychology formalizes estimation with tests and interviews. The word suits it because the result is a score rather than a diagnosis — a valuation, not a cure.
senses.whyCN: 心理学用测试与面谈把“估计”形式化。这个词合适，因为结果是一个分数而不是诊断——是估值，不是治疗。

senses.title: Damages fixed by a court
senses.titleCN: 法律上的损害赔偿评定：由法院核定一个金额
senses.definition: (law) the fixing of the amount of damages or costs by a court
senses.definitionCN: （法律）由法院核定损害赔偿或诉讼费用的金额
senses.example: The court adjourned for an assessment of the damages.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭休庭以评定损害赔偿额。
senses.why: Here assessment is the legal heir of the tax sense: a sum owed must be determined by an authority before it can be paid. The old 'fix the amount' survives intact in court language.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 assessment 是税务义的法律后代：一笔应付之款必须先由权威确定，才能支付。“把数额定下来”的旧义在法庭语言里原样存活。

intro.en: Assessment is assess plus -ment. Assess came from a Latin verb for sitting beside someone: the judge's assistant sat by to help, and one duty was fixing fines and taxes. From that seated arithmetic English took the noun in the 1530s.
intro.cn: assessment 是 assess 加 -ment。assess 来自一个表示“坐在某人旁边”的拉丁动词：法官的助手坐在旁边帮忙，其中一项职责是核定罚金与税款。英语在 16 世纪 30 年代从这个“坐着算账”的动作取走了名词。

items.en: The root *sed- 'to sit' is the reconstructed source of Latin sedere 'to sit'. No written PIE record survives, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *sed-“坐”是拉丁 sedere“坐”的重构来源。没有 PIE 书面记录留存，这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: assidere / adsidere 'to sit beside' joins ad 'to' and sedere 'to sit'; its past participle assessus means 'a sitting by'. One duty of the judge's assistant was to fix the amount of a fine or tax.
items.cn: assidere / adsidere“坐在旁边”由 ad“向”与 sedere“坐”构成；其过去分词 assessus 义为“坐在旁边”。法官助手的一项职责就是核定罚金或税款。

items.en: Medieval Latin assessare 'fix a tax upon' is originally a frequentative of assessus, and Anglo-French assesser carries it to English law.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 assessare“对……定税”原为 assessus 的反复动词，英吉利法语 assesser 把它带进英国法律。

items.en: The verb assess is recorded as 'to fix the amount of a tax or fine'. The image is still a person seated next to another, working out what is owed.
items.cn: 动词 assess 记录为“确定税款或罚金的数额”。意象仍然是一个人坐在另一个人旁边，算清欠多少。

items.en: Assessment enters in the 1530s as 'value of property for tax purposes'; the 'act of determining or adjusting a tax rate, charge or damages' follows in the 1540s, earlier carried by assession.
items.cn: assessment 于 16 世纪 30 年代进入英语，义为“供征税用的财产价值”；“确定或调整税率、费用或损害赔偿的行为”于 16 世纪 40 年代跟上，此前由 assession 承担。

items.en: The general sense 'estimation' is recorded from the 1620s; assess gains 'estimate property value for taxing' in 1809 and 'judge the value of a person or idea' in 1934; assessment becomes education jargon by 1956.
items.cn: 泛指的“估计”义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代；assess 于 1809 年获得“为征税估算财产价值”义，1934 年获得“评判人或想法的价值”义；assessment 于 1956 年成为教育行话。

note.en: The first group is a spelling trap: assignment and assistance begin like assessment but come from signum 'mark' and sistere 'stand'. The second group shares the act of valuing.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写陷阱：assignment 与 assistance 开头像 assessment，却分别来自 signum“记号”和 sistere“站立”。第二组共享“估值”这个动作。

entries.definition: a task given to someone. From assign, Latin ad- plus signum 'mark', meaning 'mark out for someone'. Not related to sitting beside.
entries.definitionCN: 任务；作业。来自 assign，即拉丁 ad- 加 signum“记号”，义为“指派给某人”，与“坐在旁边”无关。

entries.definition: help given to someone. From Latin assistere 'stand beside' (ad- + sistere 'stand'), a different verb from assidere 'sit beside'.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助；协助。来自拉丁 assistere“站在旁边”（ad- + sistere“站”），与 assidere“坐在旁边”是不同的动词。

entries.definition: to value or judge something, especially for tax. Remove -ment and the seated official remains.
entries.definitionCN: 评估；核定税额。去掉 -ment，那位坐着办事的官员还在。

entries.definition: an official who values property for tax, or an expert who judges a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 估税员；评估专家；理赔定损员。

entries.definition: the act of judging something's value or quality, often systematically.
entries.definitionCN: 评估；评价。常指系统地判断价值或质量。

entries.definition: a formal estimate of value, especially of property or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 估价；鉴定。尤指对财产或表现的正式估值。

entries.definition: a judgement or opinion of value, or a rough calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 估计；判断；粗略计算。

entries.definition: an estimate of how much money something is worth.
entries.definitionCN: 估值；定价。对某物值多少钱的估算。

entries.definition: a critical survey of something's quality or progress.
entries.definitionCN: 审查；评议。对质量或进展的批判性检视。

normalIntro.en: The word began at a tax table: as- (beside) + sess (sit) + -ment. Everything it later names — school work, health, damage, character — is valued from that seat.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起于一张税桌：as-（旁边）+ sess（坐）+ -ment。它后来命名的一切——学业、健康、损坏、人品——都是从那个座位上被估出来的。

normal.en: assess = as- (ad, beside) + sess (sedere, sit): the official sits beside you to fix your tax.
normal.cn: assess = as-（ad，旁边）+ sess（sedere，坐）：官员坐在你旁边，把你的税定下来。

normal.en: -ment turns the sitting and figuring into the figure itself: assess becomes assessment.
normal.cn: -ment 把“坐着算”变成算出的那个数：assess 成了 assessment。

normal.en: assessment and assignment look alike but split: assign comes from signum 'mark', assess from sedere 'sit'.
normal.cn: assessment 与 assignment 形似而分家：assign 来自 signum“记号”，assess 来自 sedere“坐”。

normal.en: A tax assessment, a risk assessment and a pain assessment all put a number on something.
normal.cn: 税额核定、风险评估、疼痛评估，都是给某物定一个数。

normal.en: In school, assessment is the tax office of learning: it values the work.
normal.cn: 在学校里，assessment 就是学习界的税务局：它给作业估值。

abstract.en: To assess is to sit beside a thing and decide what it is worth; the noun is that seated judgement.
abstract.cn: assess 就是坐到一件事旁边，判断它值多少；名词就是那个“坐着作出的判断”。

abstract.en: Every assessment creates a figure where there was only an impression.
abstract.cn: 每一项评估都在原本只有印象的地方造出一个数。

abstract.en: The word began at a tax table and ends in classrooms, hospitals and courts: valuation travels.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于税桌，终于教室、医院和法庭：估值一路旅行。

examples.en: The report gives a balanced assessment of the company's prospects.
examples.cn: 这份报告对公司的前景作了平衡的评估。

examples.en: Property owners have thirty days to appeal the assessment.
examples.cn: 业主有三十天时间对税额核定提出申诉。

examples.en: The course is graded by continuous assessment rather than a final exam.
examples.cn: 这门课按平时测评给分，而不是靠期末考试。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: as（在旁边）+ sess（坐）+ ment（名词）——坐在旁边把数额定下来，就是“评估、估价”，官方定下的那一笔就是“税额核定”。

root: 源自 assess + -ment；assess 于 15 世纪初借自英吉利法语 assesser ← 中世纪拉丁 assessare“对……定税”，原为拉丁 assessus（assidere“坐在旁边”的过去分词，ad- + sedere“坐”）的反复形式；原景是法官助手坐在纳税人旁边核定税款。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses start from one seated official: he looks at the property, fixes a sum, and writes it down. Remove the tax and the same structure remains — a paper valued, a patient weighed, a loss priced, a person judged.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从同一位坐着的官员开始：他看财产、定一个数、写下来。把税拿掉，结构仍在——给文章估值、给病人量分、给损失定价、给人下判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an assessor seated at a table with the tax book open, fixing a sum.
core.cn: 核心意象：估税员坐在桌前，税册摊开，把一个数额定下来。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND TAX: a value estimated, and the sum an authority demands.
branches.cn: 财产与税：被估出的价值，以及官方要求缴纳的数额。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT AND REPORT: the general act of judging, and the paper that carries it.
branches.cn: 判断与报告：泛指的评判行为，以及承载它的那份纸。

branches.en: EDUCATION AND PSYCHOLOGY: a pupil's work measured, and a mind assessed by tests.
branches.cn: 教育与心理：被量的学生作业，以及用测试评估的心智。

branches.en: MEDICINE AND INSURANCE: a condition weighed, and a loss priced.
branches.cn: 医学与保险：被权衡的病情，以及被定价的损失。

branches.en: OPINION AND LAW: an impression of a person, and damages fixed by a court.
branches.cn: 看法与法律：对人的印象，以及由法院核定的赔偿额。

intro.en: Assessment is a suffix chain on a Latin verb: assess (as- + sess) plus -ment. The same root yields assessor, assessable, reassessment and the law-French branch assessee.
intro.cn: assessment 是在一个拉丁动词上的后缀链：assess（as- + sess）加 -ment。同一词根还长出 assessor、assessable、reassessment，以及法律法语分支 assessee。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the core: ad- 'to' plus sedere 'to sit', whose participle assessus produced assessare and then English assess. The -ment is Latin -mentum through French; sed- also appears in session and sediment, where the 'sitting' idea has gone quiet.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出核心：ad-“向”加 sedere“坐”，其分词 assessus 生出 assessare，再进入英语作 assess。-ment 是经法语的拉丁 -mentum；sed- 也出现在 session、sediment 里，那里“坐”的意象已经沉睡了。

items.meaning: the act of valuing, or the valuation made
items.meaningCN: 评估的行为，或作出的估值
items.example: The assessment of the damage took two days.
items.exampleCN: 损失评估花了两天。

items.meaning: to sit beside and fix a sum; to value
items.meaningCN: 坐在旁边核定数额；评估
items.example: An expert assessed the painting at a million.
items.exampleCN: 一位专家把这幅画估到一百万。

items.meaning: one who assesses, especially for tax or insurance
items.example: The assessor measured every room.
items.exampleCN: 评估员量了每一个房间。

items.meaning: liable to be valued or taxed
items.example: The land is assessable at its market value.
items.exampleCN: 这块地应按市价计征。

items.meaning: a fresh valuation
items.example: The flood led to a reassessment of the risk.
items.exampleCN: 这场洪水导致风险被重新评估。

items.meaning: valuing one's own work or declaring one's own tax
items.meaningCN: 自我评估；自行申报纳税
items.example: Taxpayers file a self-assessment each year.
items.exampleCN: 纳税人每年自行申报一次。

items.meaning: a valuation or tax set too high
items.meaningCN: 估价过高；税额核定过高
items.example: The company appealed against an overassessment.
items.exampleCN: 公司对过高的税额核定提出申诉。

items.meaning: a person whose property is assessed
items.example: The assessee refused to sign the notice.
items.exampleCN: 被估税人拒绝在通知上签字。

items.meaning: a sitting of a court or assembly
items.meaningCN: 会议；开庭；一场（坐下来的）会期
items.example: The court held a short session that morning.
items.exampleCN: 法庭那天上午开了一次短庭。

latinEntries.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_zh: 任务；作业；分配；任命；派驻；转让
definition_en: the act of marking something out for a particular person or use, and the task, post, or right that is handed over by that act
core_image: 有人在一张名单或契据上做记号，把某件工作、某个职位或某项权利圈到另一个人名下
scene: A professor writes a chapter number beside a student's name; in another building a clerk signs a clause that moves a patent to a new owner. Both gestures are the same: a thing is marked out and made to belong to someone. That signature is an assignment of the patent.
sceneCN: 这里 assignment 是「转让」（第 6 个义项：把权利改记到别人名下）；句意：教授在学生名字旁写下章节号，另一栋楼里职员签字把专利转给新主人，这个签字就是专利的转让。场景要点：学生名单、章节号、条款文件、签字笔。

pos.zh: 任务；作业；分配；任命；转让

senses.title: The work marked out for you
senses.titleCN: 任务：被划到你名下的那份工作
senses.definition: a piece of work or a duty given to a particular person as part of a job
senses.definitionCN: 作为工作的一部分派给某人的一项工作或职责
senses.example: The reporter's assignment was to cover the flood for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这名记者的任务是连续三天报道洪灾。
senses.why: 'A task assigned, commission' is recorded by 1848, growing out of the older sense 'order, directive'. The paper that orders you to do a thing ends up naming the thing to be done.
senses.whyCN: “派给的任务、委任”义记录于 1848 年，是从更早的“命令、指令”义长出来的：那张命令你做事的纸，最后变成了要做的那件事本身。

senses.title: The school exercise carried home
senses.titleCN: 作业：带回家完成的那份课业
senses.definition: a piece of work given to a student to complete outside class
senses.definitionCN: 教师布置给学生课外完成的课业
senses.example: She finished the assignment on the bus and handed it in early.
senses.exampleCN: 她在公交车上写完了作业，提前交了上去。
senses.why: Schoolroom usage narrowed the 1848 'task assigned' to the exercise a teacher lays on a pupil. The word kept its passive flavour: an assignment is imposed, not chosen.
senses.whyCN: 校园用法把 1848 年“派给的任务”窄化为教师压给学生的一份练习。这个词保留了被动色彩：assignment 是被布置的，不是自己挑的。

senses.title: The act of handing out
senses.titleCN: 分配：把东西分出去的那个动作
senses.definition: the act of giving something such as work, money, or a role to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把工作、钱或角色分给某人或某群体的动作
senses.example: The assignment of funds to rural schools took two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 向乡村学校划拨资金花了两周。
senses.why: Assignment is the -ment noun of action from assignare, so it first names the doing rather than the thing done. Latin adsignare meant 'to mark out', and shares were allotted by ticking names against them.
senses.whyCN: assignment 是 assignare 的 -ment 动作名词，所以它先指“做这件事”，而不是“做成的东西”。拉丁语 adsignare 意为“标出来”，分配就是靠把名字与份额一一对上记号来完成的。

senses.title: A place marked with your name
senses.titleCN: 任命：在职位旁写下你的名字
senses.definition: an appointment to an office or position
senses.definitionCN: 对某个官职或职位的任命
senses.example: His assignment as ambassador was announced in March.
senses.exampleCN: 他被任命为大使的消息在三月公布。
senses.why: Recorded from mid-15c. for 'appointment to office'. A post is a slot already marked out in an institution; assigning a person to it is writing his name into that slot.
senses.whyCN: “任命职位”义记录于 15 世纪中叶。职位本就是机构里早已划好的格子；把人 assign 过去，就是把他的名字写进那个格子。

senses.title: The posting abroad
senses.titleCN: 派驻：被拴在异国岗位上的那段任期
senses.definition: a posting or tour of duty in a particular place, especially for a diplomat, soldier, or journalist
senses.definitionCN: 尤指外交官、军人或记者在某地的一段派驻任期
senses.example: After two assignments in Asia, she asked for a desk job at headquarters.
senses.exampleCN: 在亚洲两度派驻之后，她申请了总部的内勤岗位。
senses.why: A posting merges the duty with the place. The same noun names what you must do and where you must do it, because the institution has marked out that place as yours for a time.
senses.whyCN: 派驻把“职责”和“地点”合成一个词：同一个名词既指你要做的事，也指你必须去做事的地方，因为机构已经把那个地点在限定时间内划给了你。

senses.title: A right marked over to another name
senses.titleCN: 转让：把权利改记到别人名下
senses.definition: the transfer of a right, title, or interest in property to another person
senses.definitionCN: 将财产上的权利、所有权或权益转移给他人
senses.example: The assignment of the lease requires the landlord's consent.
senses.exampleCN: 转让这份租约需要房东同意。
senses.why: Assign entered English c.1300 as a legal term for conveying property, and assignment carried that sense from its first appearance. A right moves when a new holder is marked on the deed.
senses.whyCN: assign 约 1300 年作为转让财产的法律术语进入英语，assignment 从最初出现就带着这个义项。权利是靠在地契上标出新持有人而移动的。

senses.title: The paper that carries the transfer
senses.titleCN: 转让证书：承载这次转让的那张纸
senses.definition: the document by which a right or property is transferred
senses.definitionCN: 用以转让某项权利或财产的文书
senses.example: The original assignment was filed with the county clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 转让证书原件已交县书记官存档。
senses.why: English -ment nouns often name both the act and its instrument. Once a transfer had to be written down, the deed itself took the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -ment 名词常同时指动作和动作的凭据。转让一旦必须落成文字，那张契据本身也就用了这个动作的名字。

senses.title: Money set apart for a purpose
senses.titleCN: 划拨：被指定用途的那笔钱
senses.definition: the allocation of money, resources, or time to a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把资金、资源或时间指定用于某一用途
senses.example: The committee approved the assignment of emergency funds to the north.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会批准将应急资金划拨给北部。
senses.why: This is the old 'mark out' sense surviving in modern budgets: a sum is assigned when a line is drawn around it and a purpose written beside it.
senses.whyCN: 这是古老的“标出来”义在现代预算里的样子：一笔钱被圈出来、旁边写上用途，它就被 assign 了。

senses.title: A value written into a symbol
senses.titleCN: 赋值：把值写进一个符号里
senses.definition: the giving of a value, role, or task to a symbol, variable, or element in mathematics, logic, or computing
senses.definitionCN: 在数学、逻辑或计算中给符号、变量或元素指定值、角色或任务
senses.example: Each variable received a fixed assignment before the program ran.
senses.exampleCN: 程序运行前，每个变量都被赋予一个固定值。
senses.why: In logic and computing the noun keeps the purest sense of assignare: a mark placed on a symbol to fix what it shall stand for. Nothing is handed over; a value is simply written in.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑与计算中，这个词保留了 assignare 最纯粹的义：在符号上做一个记号，固定它代表什么。并没有东西被交付，只是一个值被写了进去。

intro.en: Assignment is assign plus the noun suffix -ment, and assign itself is ad- 'to' plus signare 'to make a sign', from signum 'mark'. The suffix adds an act to the verb, so the word began as 'the marking out' and then slid to the order, the duty ordered, the post, and the right transferred.
intro.cn: assignment 是 assign 加名词后缀 -ment；assign 本身是 ad-“向”加 signare“做记号”，来自 signum“记号”。后缀把动作加在动词上，所以这个词始于“标出来的动作”，再滑向命令、被命令的任务、职位，以及被转让的权利。

items.en: Signum meant 'identifying mark, sign', and signare 'to make a sign, mark'. The family is physical before it is legal: a mark is something you can see on a surface.
items.cn: signum 意为“识别性的记号、标志”，signare 意为“做记号、标记”。这个词族先有物理义，再有法律义：记号是你能在表面上看见的东西。

items.en: Assignare (also adsignare) meant 'to mark out, allot by sign, assign, award', built from ad- 'to' plus signare. The allotting was done by marking each share with its owner's name.
items.cn: assignare（也作 adsignare）意为“标出、按记号分配、授予”，由 ad-“向”加 signare 构成。分配的办法，就是在每一份上标出主人的名字。
