items.en: Assigner meant 'to assign, set a date; appoint legally; allot', and its noun assignement named a legal assignment, especially of dower. Old French passed both verb and noun to English.
items.cn: assigner 意为“分配、定日期；依法任命；分给”，其名词 assignement 指法律上的让与，尤指亡夫遗产的分配。古法语把动词和名词一起传给了英语。

items.en: Assign enters English as a legal word: 'to transfer, convey, bequeath property; appoint a task; fix a time; point out'. Its first habitat was the transfer of personal property.
items.cn: assign 作为法律词进入英语：“转让、让与、遗赠财产；指派任务；确定时间；指出”。它最初的栖身之地是动产的转让。

items.en: Assignment appears as 'an order, request, directive', from Old French assignement and Late Latin assignamentum, a noun of action from assignare. 'Appointment to office' follows in mid-15c.
items.cn: assignment 以“命令、请求、指令”义出现，来自古法语 assignement 与晚期拉丁语 assignamentum——assignare 的动作名词。“任命职位”义在 15 世纪中叶随后出现。

items.en: The modern sense 'a task assigned, commission' is recorded by 1848, and schooling made it the everyday word for homework. The legal sense never left, so one noun now covers a duty, a lesson, a posting, and a transferred right.
items.cn: 现代义“派给的任务、委任”记录于 1848 年，学校教育又使它成为“作业”的日常说法。法律义从未离开，于是同一个名词如今兼指职责、课业、派驻和转让的权利。

note.en: The look-alike group is about shared -ment endings and near spellings, not shared roots; only assignation really belongs to assign. Assessment looks close but comes from assidere 'sit beside', a different family.
note.cn: 形近组看的是共同的 -ment 词尾和相近拼写，而非同源；只有 assignation 真正属于 assign。assessment 形近却来自 assidere“坐在旁边”，是另一个词族。

entries.definition: a secret meeting, especially between lovers; also the act of assigning. It shares assign but took the -ation ending.
entries.definitionCN: 幽会，尤指情人间的秘密相会；也指分配行为。它与 assign 同源，但取的是 -ation 后缀。

entries.definition: a judgment of value or quality, from assess, which rests on Latin assidere 'sit beside', not on signum.
entries.definitionCN: 对价值或质量的评估，来自 assess，其根源是拉丁语 assidere“坐在旁边”，与 signum 无关。

entries.definition: something taken for granted, from assumere 'take up'. It echoes the ending but takes nothing from assignare.
entries.definitionCN: 想当然的假定，来自 assumere“拿起”。词尾听起来相似，却与 assignare 毫无关系。

entries.definition: a piece of work to be done. It is the plainest synonym for an assignment in the job sense.
entries.definitionCN: 要完成的一项工作。在“工作任务”义上，它是最朴素的同义词。

entries.definition: the act of dividing something and giving shares. It matches assignment as the noun of action, but stresses the division.
entries.definitionCN: 分配、分摊。它对应 assignment 的动作名词义，但更强调“切开分份”。

entries.definition: an order to carry out a piece of work, or the work itself. It is an assignment given with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 委托；受命执行的工作。它是带授权的 assignment。

entries.definition: a job that sends someone to a particular place. It matches the diplomatic and military sense of assignment.
entries.definitionCN: 派驻职位。它对应 assignment 的外交与军事派驻义。

entries.definition: lessons to be done at home. It is the everyday rival of assignment in the classroom sense.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭作业。在课堂义上，它是 assignment 最常见的同义说法。

normalIntro.en: The links are structural: ad- 'to', signum 'mark', -ment 'act of'. The word literally puts a mark on a person's name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是结构性的：ad-“向”、signum“记号”、-ment“动作”。这个词字面上就是在一个人的名字上做个记号。

normal.en: assignment = as- (ad-, 'to') + sign ('mark') + -ment: a mark placed beside your name.
normal.cn: assignment = as-（ad-，“向”）+ sign（“记号”）+ -ment：在你名字旁做的一个记号。

normal.en: The same sign- family runs through signal, signature, design and designate.
normal.cn: 同一个 sign- 词族贯穿 signal、signature、design、designate。

normal.en: A homework assignment is literally 'the task marked onto you'.
normal.cn: homework assignment 字面上就是“标到你身上的那份任务”。

normal.en: In law the assignment is both the transfer and the paper that proves it.
normal.cn: 在法律里，assignment 既是转让行为，也是证明转让的那张纸。

normal.en: In code, assigning a value means writing a mark into a variable's slot.
normal.cn: 在编程中，给变量赋值就是把一个记号写进变量的格子里。

abstract.en: A mark on a surface becomes a claim on a person: the sign is how ownership is written.
abstract.cn: 表面上的一个记号，变成对人的一项指派：记号就是所有权被写下来的方式。

abstract.en: One word holds the whole chain from 'I order you' to 'this is yours' to 'that is now his'.
abstract.cn: 一个词装下了整条链：从“我命令你”，到“这是你的”，再到“这现在是他的”。

abstract.en: Assignment always implies an outside hand: someone else drew the circle you must work inside.
abstract.cn: assignment 总含有一只外来的手：是别人画好了你必须在其内工作的那个圈。

examples.en: Her first assignment abroad was to a small embassy in West Africa.
examples.cn: 她第一次外派，是去西非的一个小使馆。

examples.en: The assignment of the family land to the eldest son was disputed for years.
examples.cn: 把家族土地转让给长子的安排，争了多年。

examples.en: Students who miss class can download the assignment from the course page.
examples.cn: 缺课的学生可以从课程页面下载作业。

dict_mnemonic.text: as（去）+ sign（记号）+ ment（名词）——去在名单上做个记号，把任务划给某人；谐音“额塞门特”：额（我）塞（sign）进门槛（ment），领到那份任务 → assignment 任务；分配

root: 源自拉丁语 assignare（ad-“向”+ signare“做记号”，来自 signum“记号”），经古法语 assigner 进入英语；-ment 为动作名词后缀，核心是“按记号把某物划归某人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: making a mark. The mark first assigns a share, then a duty, then a classroom exercise, then a post, then a right on a deed, and finally a value inside a symbol.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着同一个动作展开：做记号。这个记号先分出份额，再分出职责，再变成课堂作业、派驻职位、地契上的权利，最后写进一个符号里的值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark made beside a name — something is pointed out and thereby made to belong to someone.
core.cn: 核心意象：在名字旁做下的一个记号——某物被指出来，因而归到了某人名下。

chain: NAME A PERSON FOR A POST
THE RIGHT MOVED TO A NEW HOLDER
FIX A VALUE ON A SYMBOL

branches.en: THE TASK ITSELF: the work marked out for an employee, and the exercise marked out for a pupil.
branches.cn: 任务本身：给职员划出的工作，以及给学生划出的课业。

branches.en: ALLOTTING: the act of sharing out in general, and the earmarking of money for a purpose.
branches.cn: 分配动作：一般意义上的分发，以及把钱指定用于某一用途。

branches.en: THE POST: a slot in an institution, and the foreign place where that slot sits for a term.
branches.cn: 职位：机构里的一个格子，以及这个格子在国外落址的一段任期。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: the moving of a right to a new holder, and the deed that records the move.
branches.cn: 转让：把权利移到新持有人名下，以及记录这次移动的契据。

branches.en: THE MARK ON A SYMBOL: a value written into a variable, with nothing handed over at all.
branches.cn: 符号上的记号：写进变量的一个值，完全没有东西被交付。

intro.en: Assignment is assign plus -ment. The base assign is ad- plus sign-, and the -ment turns the verb into the act or its result, which is why one word can mean the assigning and the thing assigned.
intro.cn: assignment 是 assign 加 -ment。基础词 assign 是 ad- 加 sign-，而 -ment 把动词变成动作或动作的结果，所以同一个词既能指“分配”，也能指“被分配之物”。

latinIntro.en: Latin signum 'mark' and signare 'to mark' supply the whole sign- family. With ad- they yield assignare; with de- designare and designare's English child design; with con- consignare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 signum“记号”与 signare“做记号”供给整个 sign- 词族。加 ad- 得 assignare；加 de- 得 designare，并在英语里生出 design；加 con- 得 consignare。

items.meaning: to mark out for someone; to allot or appoint
items.meaningCN: 分配给；指派（标到某人名下）
items.example: The teacher assigned each group a different poem.
items.exampleCN: 老师给每个小组指派了不同的诗。

items.meaning: the act of allotting; the task or right allotted
items.meaningCN: 分配；被分派的任务或权利
items.example: The assignment was posted online at noon.
items.exampleCN: 任务中午被发布到了网上。

items.meaning: a mark that stands for something
items.example: A stop sign marks where cars must halt.
items.exampleCN: 停车标志标出车辆必须停下的地方。

items.meaning: a mark or gesture that conveys a message
items.example: The lighthouse sends a signal every ten seconds.
items.exampleCN: 灯塔每十秒发出一次信号。

items.meaning: a person's name written as a mark
items.example: Her signature appears on every page of the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 条约每一页上都有她的签名。

items.meaning: to mark out officially; to name
items.example: The council designated the old mill a heritage site.
items.exampleCN: 议会指定这座老磨坊为遗产地。

items.meaning: to mark out a plan; a plan so marked
items.example: She designed the garden around a single oak.
items.exampleCN: 她围绕一棵橡树设计了这座花园。

items.meaning: to mark goods for delivery; to entrust
items.meaningCN: 托运；交付（给货物做记号）
items.example: The crates were consigned to a warehouse in Leeds.
items.exampleCN: 这些板条箱被托运到利兹的一处仓库。

items.meaning: the person to whom a right is transferred
items.meaningCN: 受让人（接受权利转移的人）
items.example: The assignee must sign before the transfer is valid.
items.exampleCN: 受让人必须先签字，转让才有效。

items.meaning: the person who transfers a right
items.example: The assignor retains no interest in the patent.
items.exampleCN: 转让人对该专利不再保留任何权益。

latinEntries.meaning: to mark out, allot by sign

definition_zh: 帮助；援助；协助；助力装置；司法协助
definition_en: the act of standing by someone to lend a hand, and the help, support, or device that is supplied
core_image: 一个人原本独自站着，另一个人走到他身旁站定，伸出手去
scene: A car dies on a mountain road. A stranger pulls over, walks to the open hood, and stands beside the driver with a torch. Nothing is taken away; someone simply takes a stand next to someone else. The stranger's assistance costs nothing more than standing beside the driver with a torch.
sceneCN: 这里 assistance 是「帮助」（第 1 个义项：站到旁边、伸出手）；句意：车在山路上熄火，陌生人把车停下，拿着手电站到司机身边，这种帮助不过是站在旁边照个亮。场景要点：山路、熄火的车、掀开的引擎盖、手电、陌生人。

pos.zh: 帮助；援助；协助；助力装置

derivatives.zh: （研究生）助教奖学金；助理职位

senses.title: Standing by to lend a hand
senses.titleCN: 帮助：站到旁边，伸出手
senses.definition: the act of helping someone do something
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人做某事的动作
senses.example: She asked her neighbour for assistance with the heavy boxes.
senses.exampleCN: 她请邻居帮忙搬那些沉重的箱子。
senses.why: Early 15c., 'act of helping or aiding', from Medieval Latin assistentia, from assistere 'stand by'. Help begins as a posture: you first take a stand beside the person who needs it.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪初的“帮助、援助行为”来自中世纪拉丁语 assistentia，而后者出自 assistere“站在旁边”。帮助始于一个姿势：你先站到需要帮助的人身边。

senses.title: Aid you can spend
senses.titleCN: 援助：能拨款、能花出去的那种帮助
senses.definition: money, equipment, or other material help given to people who need it
senses.definitionCN: 给予需要者的钱、设备或其他物质帮助
senses.example: The government offered financial assistance to first-time farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 政府向首次务农者提供经济援助。
senses.why: Modern welfare and administrative language made the abstract act countable and spendable. Assistance became the thing a budget hands over, not only the gesture of standing near.
senses.whyCN: 现代福利与行政语言把这个抽象动作变得可数、可花。assistance 成了预算可以拨付的东西，而不只是“站在旁边”的姿势。

senses.title: Help in an emergency
senses.titleCN: 救助：危急时刻伸出的那只手
senses.definition: urgent help given to someone in danger or serious difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 给予身处危险或严重困境者的紧急帮助
senses.example: The climbers waved for assistance from the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 登山者在山脊上挥手求救。
senses.why: The noun narrows when the context is danger: the one who stands by becomes the one who runs in. English marks the urgency through collocation — call for, need, come to — not through a new word.
senses.whyCN: 语境一涉及危险，这个词就窄化了：原本站在旁边的人，变成冲进去的人。英语靠搭配（call for、need、come to）来标记这份紧急，而不另造新词。

senses.title: The hand at the side, not in front
senses.titleCN: 协助：在旁边搭手，而不是站在前头
senses.definition: secondary help that supports someone else's main effort
senses.definitionCN: 对他人主要工作的次要性支持帮助
senses.example: With the assistance of a translator, the two delegates reached an agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 在一名译员的协助下，两位代表达成了协议。
senses.why: 'With the assistance of' keeps the Latin picture visible: the helper stands beside the doer, adding a hand without taking the lead. The preposition names the source, not the chief agent.
senses.whyCN: with the assistance of 让拉丁语的画面保持可见：帮手站在做事者旁边，添一只手，却不抢主位。介词引出的是帮助的来源，而非主要施事者。

senses.title: Power assistance: help built into a machine
senses.titleCN: 助力：装进机器里的那只手
senses.definition: a mechanical or electronic aid that reduces the effort needed to operate something
senses.definitionCN: 减轻操作某物所需力气的机械或电子辅助装置
senses.example: The car's power assistance makes parking in narrow streets easy.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的动力助力让在窄街停车变得轻松。
senses.why: Twentieth-century engineering moved assistance from people to mechanisms: a pump or motor stands beside your arm, as it were, and does part of the pushing. The abstract noun becomes a name for the built-in helper.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的工程技术把 assistance 从人身上移到了机械上：泵或电机仿佛站在你手臂旁边，替你出一部分力。抽象名词于是成了这个内置帮手的名字。

senses.title: Hands-on help with daily living
senses.titleCN: 生活照料：扶在肘上的那只手
senses.definition: practical help with washing, eating, moving, or other daily activities
senses.definitionCN: 在洗漱、进食、行动等日常活动中给予的实际帮助
senses.example: He needs assistance with dressing in the mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 他早晨穿衣需要人帮忙。
senses.why: Care language measures assistance by the body: what is lent is not advice or money but a hand at the elbow. The word stays abstract while the help becomes very concrete.
senses.whyCN: 护理语言用身体来度量 assistance：借出去的不是建议或钱，而是扶在肘上的一只手。词仍是抽象的，帮助却变得极其具体。

senses.title: Institutions standing by each other
senses.titleCN: 司法协助：两个机构彼此站台
senses.definition: help given by one authority or state to another, especially in legal or police matters
senses.definitionCN: 一个当局或国家向另一个当局或国家提供的帮助，尤指法律或警务方面
senses.example: The two countries signed a treaty on mutual legal assistance.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项司法协助条约。
senses.why: In treaties the old 'stand by' sense is applied to institutions: one legal system takes a formal stand beside another. Mutual marks a symmetry that a personal favour does not have.
senses.whyCN: 在条约里，古老的“站到旁边”义被用到了机构上：一个法律体系正式站到另一个身边。mutual 标出了一种私人帮忙所没有的对等性。

senses.title: Aid that stands beside force
senses.titleCN: 支援：站在作战部队旁边的帮助
senses.definition: support given to a military or police operation, such as equipment, training, or troops
senses.definitionCN: 给予军事或警务行动的支持，如装备、训练或部队
senses.example: The mission provided medical assistance to the border units.
senses.exampleCN: 该任务为边防部队提供了医疗支援。
senses.why: Military assistance keeps the Latin attendance metaphor: supporting units take their stand near the fighting units but are not the fighting units. The noun marks a supporting role, not command.
senses.whyCN: 军事支援保留了拉丁语“侍立”的隐喻：支援单位站到作战单位旁边，却并不等于作战单位。这个名词标出的是一种辅助角色，而非指挥权。

senses.title: Attendance: the oldest sense of standing by
senses.titleCN: 侍立：最古老的“站在旁边”
senses.definition: the state of attending upon or standing by a person of rank (historical)
senses.definitionCN: 侍奉或随侍在显贵身边的状态（历史义）
senses.example: In the chronicle, the knights are listed among the king's assistance.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史中，这些骑士被列在国王的随侍之列。
senses.why: Latin assistere meant 'stand by, attend', and Medieval Latin assistentia could name the mere presence of attendants. The helpful sense grew out of this courtly standing-near, which is why the word never quite loses its posture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 assistere 意为“站在旁边、随侍”，中世纪拉丁语 assistentia 可以指侍从单纯的在场。“帮助”义正是从这种宫廷式的近身侍立长出来的，所以这个词始终没丢掉它的姿势。

intro.en: Assistance is assist plus -ance. Assist comes from Latin assistere, ad- 'to' plus sistere 'to stand', and -ance turns the verb into the state or act of doing it. The shift is from presence to help: first you stand beside someone, then you lend a hand, then you supply money or equipment.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 加 -ance。assist 来自拉丁语 assistere，即 ad-“向”加 sistere“站立”，而 -ance 把动词变成做这件事的状态或动作。语义从“在场”移向“帮助”：先站到某人旁边，再搭把手，再提供钱或设备。

items.en: Sistere meant 'stand still, take a stand; set, place, cause to stand', from PIE *si-st-, a reduplicated form of *sta- 'to stand'. That Indo-European layer is a reconstruction with no written record and is therefore marked source uncertain; the root is about feet and position, not about taking or holding.
items.cn: sistere 意为“站住、站定；放置、使站立”，来自印欧语 *si-st-，是 *sta-“站立”的重复形式。这一印欧语层是没有书面记录的重构，故标为“来源不确定”；这个词根讲的是脚和位置，与“拿取”无关。

items.en: Assistere meant 'stand by, take a stand near, attend', built from ad- 'to' plus sistere. A person described this way is not yet helping; he is simply stationed at someone's side.
items.cn: assistere 意为“站在旁边、站到近处、随侍”，由 ad-“向”加 sistere 构成。这样描述的人还谈不上帮忙，他只是被安置在某人身边。

items.en: Assister meant 'to stand by, help, put, place, assist'. Old French widened the Latin posture into a service: standing near a person came to imply doing something for him.
items.cn: 古法语 assister 意为“站在旁边、帮助、放置、协助”。古法语把拉丁语的姿势扩大为一种服务：站到某人身边，逐渐意味着为他做点什么。

items.en: Assist enters English as 'to help, aid, give assistance or support to in some undertaking or effort'. The physical sense of standing by has already become the social sense of helping.
items.cn: assist 以“帮助、援助、在某项事业或努力中给予支持”义进入英语。身体上的“站在旁边”已经变成了社会性的“帮忙”。

items.en: Assistance comes from Old French assistance and Medieval Latin assistentia, the abstract noun of the verb. The -ance suffix names the act or state, and the earliest recorded meaning is simply 'act of helping or aiding'.
items.cn: assistance 来自古法语 assistance 与中世纪拉丁语 assistentia，即该动词的抽象名词。-ance 后缀命名动作或状态，最早记录的意义就是“帮助、援助的行为”。

items.en: Later centuries made the noun concrete: financial and technical assistance, mutual legal assistance, and finally power assistance built into vehicles. Each is the same 'standing by' handed to a budget, a treaty, or a machine.
items.cn: 后来的世纪让这个名词具体化：经济与技术援助、司法协助，最后是装进车辆里的动力助力。每一种都还是同一个“站在旁边”，只是交给了预算、条约或机器。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sist- root and the -ance/-ant endings. Resistance and insistence are true sisters of assist, built on the same sistere with different prefixes; only their meanings diverge.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sist- 词根与 -ance/-ant 词尾。resistance 与 insistence 确实是 assist 的同族，用同一个 sistere 配不同前缀，只是意义分开了。

entries.definition: a person who helps another in a job. It is the person-noun of assistance, made with -ant instead of -ance.
entries.definitionCN: 助手；助理。它是 assistance 的人称名词，用 -ant 而不是 -ance。

entries.definition: to help someone. It is the bare verb that assistance wraps in an abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助；协助。它是 assistance 包上抽象名词外壳之前的光秃动词。

entries.definition: the act of standing against something. Same sistere 'stand', but re- turns standing beside into standing against.
entries.definitionCN: 抵抗；反抗。同一个 sistere“站立”，但 re- 把“站在旁边”变成了“站在对面”。

entries.definition: the act of standing firmly on a demand. Again sistere, with in- placing the stance upon something.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持；坚决要求。还是 sistere，只是 in- 把站姿压在某件事上。

entries.definition: help, especially money or supplies given to people in need. It leans toward the material sense of assistance.
entries.definitionCN: 援助，尤指给需要者的钱或物资。它偏向 assistance 的物质义。

entries.definition: the act of making it easier for someone to do something. It is the plain native synonym, with no Latin posture attached.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助。它是最朴素的本族语同义词，不带拉丁语的站姿。

entries.definition: help that holds someone or something up. It stresses bearing weight, where assistance stresses standing near.
entries.definitionCN: 支持；支撑。它强调承重，而 assistance 强调站在旁边。

entries.definition: aid given to people in hardship. It names the lifting of a burden, not the presence of a helper.
entries.definitionCN: 救济；缓解。它命名的是卸下负担，而不是帮手在场。

entries.definition: extra help held ready behind the main effort. It matches the secondary, stand-by sense of assistance.
entries.definitionCN: 后备支援。它对应 assistance 那次要、待命的一层。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: ad- 'to', sistere 'stand', -ance 'state of'. The word is a posture before it is a service.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：ad-“向”、sistere“站立”、-ance“状态”。这个词先是姿势，后是服务。

normal.en: assistance = as- (ad-, 'to') + sist ('stand') + -ance: standing next to someone.
normal.cn: assistance = as-（ad-，“向”）+ sist（“站”）+ -ance：站到某人旁边。

normal.en: The sist- family is a row of stances: assist, insist, resist, persist, exist.
normal.cn: sist- 词族是一排站姿：assist、insist、resist、persist、exist。

normal.en: An assistant is the person who takes that stand; assistance is the standing itself.
normal.cn: assistant 是采取那个站姿的人；assistance 是那个站姿本身。

normal.en: Financial assistance is money taught to stand beside you.
normal.cn: financial assistance 是被教会站到你身边的钱。

normal.en: Power assistance is a motor standing at your elbow.
normal.cn: power assistance 是站在你肘边的一台电机。

abstract.en: Help is drawn as geometry: one body placed beside another, sharing the load at the point of contact.
abstract.cn: 帮助被画成几何：一具身体放在另一具旁边，在接触点上分担重量。

abstract.en: The word never names the work, only the position — which is why it can be lent to money, law, or machinery.
abstract.cn: 这个词从不命名具体工作，只命名位置——所以它能被借给金钱、法律或机械。

abstract.en: Assistance implies you are not alone, without promising that the burden gets lighter.
abstract.cn: assistance 意味着你不是一个人，但并不保证担子会变轻。

examples.en: Without assistance, the small clinic could not have stayed open through the winter.
examples.cn: 没有援助，这家小诊所根本撑不过冬天。

examples.en: He rebuilt the engine with the assistance of an old manual.
examples.cn: 他借助一本旧手册重新装好了发动机。

examples.en: The airline offers assistance to passengers who cannot walk long distances.
examples.cn: 这家航空公司为走不了长距离的乘客提供协助。

dict_mnemonic.text: as（去）+ sist（站）+ ance（名词）——走过去站在他旁边，就是帮忙；谐音“额西斯腾斯”：额（我）西斯（sist）腾（ance）出手，站到旁边搭把手 → assistance 帮助；援助

root: 源自拉丁语 assistere（ad-“向”+ sistere“站立、站定”），经古法语 assister 进入英语；-ance 为抽象名词后缀，核心是“站到某人旁边”，由在场随侍引申为帮助。sistere 与 assume 的 sumere 无关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one stance. Someone first stands near, then lends a hand; the hand becomes money, becomes care, becomes a treaty, becomes a motor, and the oldest sense simply remembers the attendant standing at court.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一个站姿。有人先站到近处，再伸出手；这只手变成钱、变成照料、变成条约、变成马达，而最古老的义项只是记得宫廷里那个随侍站立的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: taking a stand beside someone — help begins as presence, then becomes an offered hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：站到某人旁边——帮助始于在场，然后才成为伸出的手。

branches.en: THE POSTURE: standing by and adding a hand from the side, without taking the lead.
branches.cn: 姿势：站在旁边，从侧面添一只手，却不抢主位。

branches.en: MATERIAL SUPPORT: money and equipment for civilians, kit and training for soldiers.
branches.cn: 物质支持：给平民的钱与设备，给士兵的装备与训练。

branches.en: HANDS-ON HELP: pulling someone out of danger, and helping someone dress or eat.
branches.cn: 身体力行的帮助：把人从危险里拉出来，以及帮人穿衣吃饭。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL HELP: a motor boosting an arm, a legal system standing beside another.
branches.cn: 制度化帮助：电机为手臂助力，一个法律体系站到另一个身边。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: mere attendance, the courtier standing near the throne.
branches.cn: 古老义：单纯的随侍，朝臣站在王座旁边。

intro.en: Assistance is assist plus -ance, the suffix that turns a verb into an abstract noun of action or state. Assist is ad- plus sist-, so the whole word is built from a prefix, a standing root, and a noun ending.
intro.cn: assistance 是 assist 加 -ance，这个后缀把动词变成表示动作或状态的抽象名词。assist 是 ad- 加 sist-，所以整词由前缀、表“站立”的词根和名词后缀三层构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere 'stand' is the base of a large family: assistere (stand by), insistere (stand upon), resistere (stand against), persistere (stand through), exsistere (stand out, exist), consistere (stand together).
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere“站立”是一个大词族的基础：assistere（站在旁边）、insistere（站在其上）、resistere（站在对面）、persistere（站到底）、exsistere（站出来、存在）、consistere（站在一起）。

items.meaning: to stand by; to help
items.example: Two nurses assisted the surgeon.
items.exampleCN: 两名护士协助外科医生。

items.meaning: the state or act of being helped or helping
items.meaningCN: 帮助；援助（帮助的状态或行为）
items.example: The family applied for housing assistance.
items.exampleCN: 这家人申请了住房援助。

items.meaning: one who stands by and helps
items.meaningCN: 助手（站在旁边帮忙的人）
items.example: The assistant filed the reports before noon.
items.exampleCN: 助手在中午前把报告归档了。

items.meaning: serving to help, especially of devices
items.example: Assistive technology lets him use a computer by voice.
items.exampleCN: 辅助技术让他能用语音操作电脑。

items.meaning: to stand firmly upon a demand
items.meaningCN: 坚持；坚决要求（站在某要求上）
items.example: She insisted on paying for the meal.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持要付这顿饭钱。

items.meaning: to stand against; to oppose
items.example: The old walls resisted the flood for a week.
items.exampleCN: 旧墙抗住洪水一个星期。

items.meaning: to keep standing through difficulty
items.example: The smell persisted for days after the fire.
items.exampleCN: 火灭之后那股气味持续了好几天。

items.meaning: to stand forth; to be
items.example: Such a custom existed long before the empire.
items.exampleCN: 这种习俗在帝国之前很久就存在了。

items.meaning: to stand together; to be made of
items.example: The committee consists of nine members.
items.exampleCN: 委员会由九名成员组成。

items.meaning: to stand away from; to stop
items.example: The company desisted from using the slogan.
items.exampleCN: 公司停止使用那句口号。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand still, take a stand

definition_zh: 假设；假定；前提；承担；就任；僭取；傲慢；圣母升天
definition_en: the act of taking something up onto oneself, whether a proposition treated as true, a duty or office taken on, or a right taken without warrant
core_image: 一个人伸手把桌上的东西拿起来，收进自己怀里——拿起的可能是前提、职位、责任，也可能是不属于他的权利
scene: A detective writes 'the butler did it' at the top of a page and reasons downward from it; a new minister takes up the seal of office; a guest takes a seat that is not his. Each gesture is a taking-up. The detective's first line is an assumption: the butler did it.
sceneCN: 这里 assumption 是「假设」（第 1 个义项：把某命题当作已经成立）；句意：侦探在纸页顶端写下「是管家干的」，把它当作推理的假设。场景要点：侦探的纸页、顶端的字、官印、不属于自己的座位。

pos.zh: 假设；假定；前提；承担；就任；僭取

senses.title: Taking a proposition as given
senses.titleCN: 假设：把一个命题当作已经成立
senses.definition: a belief that something is true, held without proof and used as a starting point
senses.definitionCN: 未经证明便认为某事为真，并把它当作出发点
senses.example: We planned the walk on the assumption that the weather would hold.
senses.exampleCN: 我们假定天气会持续晴好，据此安排了徒步。
senses.why: The sense 'something taken for granted' is recorded from the 1620s. The mind performs the hand's act: it takes a proposition up and lays it down as a floor to stand on.
senses.whyCN: “想当然之事”这一义记录于 17 世纪 20 年代。心智做的是手的动作：把一个命题拿起来，再放下当成站立的地板。

senses.title: The guess that forgets it is guessing
senses.titleCN: 想当然：忘了自己只是在猜
senses.definition: a supposition treated as fact, especially one made without enough evidence
senses.definitionCN: 被当作事实的推测，尤指证据不足的那种
senses.example: His assumption that everyone owned a car made the survey useless.
senses.exampleCN: 他想当然地以为人人都有车，这让调查结果毫无用处。
senses.why: Assume has meant 'suppose without proof' since the 1590s. The act is blameless while the taker remembers the object is only borrowed; it turns into a fault when he forgets.
senses.whyCN: assume 从 16 世纪 90 年代起就有“未经证明便假定”义。只要拿的人记得这东西是借来的，动作就无可指责；一旦忘了，就成了过失。

senses.title: The minor premise the argument stands on
senses.titleCN: 小前提：论证站在上面的那一句
senses.definition: a proposition accepted as the basis of an argument; the minor premise of a syllogism
senses.definitionCN: 作为论证基础而被接受的命题；三段论的小前提
senses.example: The conclusion follows only if the assumption is true.
senses.exampleCN: 只有当这个前提为真时，结论才成立。
senses.why: Late 14c. the noun named the minor premise of a syllogism, from Latin assumptio 'a taking up'. Logic takes a proposition up into the argument and lets the conclusion rest its weight on it.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪末，这个词指三段论的小前提，来自拉丁语 assumptio“拿起来”。逻辑把命题拿进论证，再让结论把重量压在它上面。

senses.title: Weight taken onto your shoulders
senses.titleCN: 承担：把重量接到自己肩上
senses.definition: the taking on of a responsibility, duty, or power
senses.definitionCN: 承担责任、义务或权力
senses.example: The assumption of debt by the buyer was written into the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 买方承担债务一事写进了合同。
senses.why: Mid-15c. 'appropriation of a right or possession'; the 1580s sense 'action of taking for oneself' widened it. A duty is assumed the way a load is taken up: it becomes yours to carry.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中叶有“占有权利或财物”义，16 世纪 80 年代“为自己拿取”义又把它拓宽。责任之被 assume，正如重物之被拿起：它变成你要扛的东西。

senses.title: Taking up the seal of office
senses.titleCN: 就任：接过官印的那一下
senses.definition: the act of taking up an office, throne, or position
senses.definitionCN: 接任职位、王位或职务的行为
senses.example: The assumption of the presidency takes place at noon on January 20.
senses.exampleCN: 总统就任在 1 月 20 日正午举行。
senses.why: An office was one of the things assumere could take up. English fixed the phrase 'assumption of office' because the ceremony is literally a taking-hold: the seal, the keys, the chair.
senses.whyCN: 职位本就是 assumere 可以拿起来的东西之一。英语固定了 assumption of office 这个说法，因为仪式字面上就是抓住：抓住官印、钥匙、座椅。

senses.title: Taking what was never given
senses.titleCN: 僭取：拿走从未给过你的东西
senses.definition: the act of taking a right, property, or power to which one has no claim
senses.definitionCN: 夺取自己本无权主张的权利、财产或权力
senses.example: The court condemned the assumption of public land by the neighbouring estate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院谴责邻庄侵占公共土地。
senses.why: Mid-15c. 'appropriation of a right or possession', from a Ciceronian Latin use. The verb can take up anything; the noun grows dark when the thing taken was never offered.
senses.whyCN: 15 世纪中叶的“占有权利或财物”义来自西塞罗式的拉丁用法。这个动词什么都能拿；当被拿之物从未被给予时，名词就变暗了。

senses.title: The bearing of one who has taken too much
senses.titleCN: 傲慢：揽得太多的人摆出的姿态
senses.definition: arrogance or presumptuousness, especially in manner (largely archaic)
senses.definitionCN: 傲慢、自以为是，尤指态度上的（今多属古义）
senses.example: He spoke with an assumption that no junior officer would dare.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话时带着一种年轻军官不敢有的傲慢。
senses.why: Latin assumptio is morally neutral, but one who takes much to himself looks puffed up. The noun for the act drifted into a name for the manner, and presumption became its everyday heir.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 assumptio 在道德上是中性的，但把太多东西揽到自己身上的人看起来就趾高气扬。指动作的名词漂移成指姿态的词，presumption 则成了它日常的继承者。

senses.title: Putting on an appearance
senses.titleCN: 装作：把一副神情穿在身上
senses.definition: the act of putting on a false appearance or manner
senses.definitionCN: 装出虚假的外表或神态
senses.example: Her assumption of calm fooled no one at the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 她在葬礼上装出的镇定谁也骗不过。
senses.why: From c.1600 assume could mean 'take or put on fictitiously', as one puts on a garment. An appearance is the lightest thing a person can take up and the easiest to take off.
senses.whyCN: 约 1600 年起，assume 可指“虚假地装出、披上”，就像穿上一件衣服。神情是一个人能拿起的最轻的东西，也最容易脱下。

senses.title: The Assumption: a body taken up
senses.titleCN: 圣母升天：被接上去的身体
senses.definition: the reception of the Virgin Mary into heaven, celebrated on 15 August
senses.definitionCN: 圣母马利亚被接升天，于 8 月 15 日庆祝
senses.example: The village holds its fair on the Feast of the Assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 村子在圣母升天节举办集市。
senses.why: The earliest English use, c.1300, is this religious one, from Latin assumptio 'a taking up'. The feast entered English church language more than a century before the verb assume did.
senses.whyCN: 最早的英语用法（约 1300 年）就是这个宗教义，来自拉丁语 assumptio“被拿上去”。这个节日的说法进入英语教会语言，比动词 assume 早一个多世纪。

intro.en: Assumption is assume plus -tion, though the noun reached English first: assumption c.1300, the verb assume only early 15c. Latin assumptio is a noun of action from assumere, ad- 'to' plus sumere 'to take'. The suffix names the act of taking up, and the meanings slide from a proposition taken as true to an office taken on to a right taken without leave.
intro.cn: assumption 是 assume 加 -tion，不过名词先到英语：assumption 约 1300 年，动词 assume 要到 15 世纪初。拉丁语 assumptio 是 assumere 的动作名词，assumere 即 ad-“向”加 sumere“拿取”。后缀命名“拿起来”这个动作，词义则从“把命题拿作真的”滑到“把职位接过来”，再到“把不属于自己的权利拿走”。

items.en: Sumere meant 'to take, take up, use up', from sub- 'under' plus emere 'to take'. Emere goes back to PIE *em- 'to take, distribute', a reconstructed root with no written record.
items.cn: sumere 意为“拿、拿起、用掉”，由 sub-“在下”加 emere“取”构成。emere 可追溯到印欧语 *em-“拿取、分配”，但这是没有书面记录的重构，因此最深层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Assumere (also adsumere) meant 'to take up, take to oneself, take besides, obtain in addition'. The ad- adds direction toward the taker, not a new object.
items.cn: assumere（也作 adsumere）意为“拿起、据为己有、额外取得、附加获得”。ad- 加的是“朝向拿取者”的方向，而不是一个新的对象。

items.en: Assumptio, from the past-participle stem assumpt-, meant 'a taking up, receiving, acceptance, adoption'. It covered both lifting a body and taking something into one's own possession, physical or legal.
items.cn: assumptio 由过去分词词干 assumpt- 构成，意为“拿起、接收、接受、采纳”。它既指物理上的举起，也指心理或法律上把某物收归己有。

items.en: The noun enters English as assumpcioun, 'the reception of the Virgin Mary into heaven', through Old French assumpcion; the Feast of the Assumption (15 August) came with it. A church festival was the word's first doorway into English.
items.cn: 这个名词以 assumpcioun 进入英语，义为“圣母马利亚被接升天”，经古法语 assumpcion 而来，同时带来 8 月 15 日的圣母升天节。宗教义就是这个词进入英语的那道门。

items.en: From late 14c. the noun also named the minor premise of a syllogism; the sense 'act of taking something to oneself, appropriation' follows in the 15c. Logic and law each took a share of the Latin 'taking up'.
items.cn: 从 14 世纪末起，这个名词也指三段论的“小前提”；“把某物收归己有的行为”义随后在 15 世纪出现。逻辑与法律各取走了拉丁语“拿起”的一份。

items.en: The verb assume enters early 15c. as 'arrogate, take upon oneself' from Latin assumere, adding 'suppose without proof' in the 1590s and 'pretend falsely' about 1600. By the 1620s the noun's everyday sense is 'something taken for granted'.
items.cn: 动词 assume 于 15 世纪初以“僭取、揽到自己身上”义从拉丁语 assumere 进入英语，16 世纪 90 年代加上“未经证明便假定”，约 1600 年又加上“虚假地装出”。到 17 世纪 20 年代，名词的日常义已是“想当然之事”。

note.en: The look-alike group is mostly genuine family: consumption, presumption and resumption all use Latin sumere 'take' with different prefixes. Assurance looks similar but comes from securus 'free from care', so it must not be dragged into this family.
note.cn: 形近组大多是真同族：consumption、presumption、resumption 都用拉丁语 sumere“拿取”配不同前缀。assurance 形似却来自 securus“无忧”，不能硬拉进这个词族。

entries.definition: the using up of goods, fuel, or energy. Same sumere 'take', with con- 'altogether' marking the using-up.
entries.definitionCN: 对商品、燃料或能量的消耗。同一个 sumere“拿取”，con-“彻底”标出“用完”。

entries.definition: a belief taken before the evidence, or boldness beyond one's place. It is assumption's close cousin, with prae- 'beforehand'.
entries.definitionCN: 证据之前就先拿定的信念，或越出本分的放肆。它是 assumption 的近亲，前缀是 prae-“ beforehand、预先”。

entries.definition: the act of taking something up again after a pause. Same root, re- 'back, again'.
entries.definitionCN: 停顿之后重新开始、重新拿起。同根，前缀 re-“回、再”。

entries.definition: a promise that removes doubt, from ad- plus securus 'free from care'. The ending matches, the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 消除疑虑的保证，来自 ad- 加 securus“无忧”。词尾相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: an idea accepted as true without proof. It is the closest formal synonym of assumption in logic.
entries.definitionCN: 未经证明便接受的想法。在逻辑义上，它是 assumption 最接近的正式同义词。

entries.definition: a proposal put forward as a possible explanation, to be tested. It is an assumption made for research.
entries.definitionCN: 作为可能解释提出、有待检验的命题。它是为研究而设的 assumption。

entries.definition: a statement from which a conclusion is drawn. It names the logical role that an assumption fills.
entries.definitionCN: 据以推出结论的陈述。它命名的是 assumption 所占据的逻辑位置。

entries.definition: an assumption treated as settled, often with a tone of arrogance. It overlaps both the logical and the arrogant sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被当作已定的假定，常带傲慢语气。它同时覆盖逻辑义与傲慢义。

entries.definition: an opinion formed without sufficient evidence. It is the plain, informal relative of an assumption.
entries.definitionCN: 证据不足时形成的看法。它是 assumption 最朴素、最口语的亲戚。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: ad- 'to', sumere 'take', -tion 'act of'. The word is a hand reaching out and pulling something toward the chest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：ad-“向”、sumere“拿取”、-tion“动作”。这个词就是一只手伸出去，把东西拉向胸口。

normal.en: assumption = as- (ad-, 'to') + sum ('take') + -ption: a taking toward oneself.
normal.cn: assumption = as-（ad-，“向”）+ sum（“拿”）+ -ption：朝自己拿过来。

normal.en: The sum- family is all taking: assume, consume, resume, presume, subsume.
normal.cn: sum- 词族都在“拿”：assume、consume、resume、presume、subsume。

normal.en: Consumption is the same taking, but with the 'use up' prefix con-.
normal.cn: consumption 是同一个“拿”，只是前缀 con- 表示“用光”。

normal.en: An assumption in an argument is something you pick up and stand on.
normal.cn: 论证里的 assumption，是你捡起来、站上去的那块板。

normal.en: The Assumption is the same word in church: a body taken up, not a claim taken on.
normal.cn: 宗教里的 the Assumption 是同一个词：被接上去的身体，而不是被揽下的主张。

abstract.en: Thinking is imagined as manual labour: the mind lifts propositions the way the arm lifts boxes.
abstract.cn: 思考被想象成体力活：心智举起命题，正如手臂举起箱子。

abstract.en: The word's danger is built into its image — what you take up may not have been offered.
abstract.cn: 这个词的危险写在它的意象里——你拿起来的东西，未必是被递给你的。

abstract.en: One gesture covers logic, law, and liturgy: to take up is to make something yours, for a moment or forever.
abstract.cn: 一个动作覆盖逻辑、法律与礼仪：拿起来，就是让某物在一瞬或永久之间归你。

examples.en: The whole model rests on a single assumption that nobody has tested.
examples.cn: 整个模型都建立在一条无人检验过的假设上。

examples.en: She took on the assumption of care for her aunt without complaint.
examples.cn: 她毫无怨言地承担起照顾姑妈的责任。

examples.en: Economists warn against the assumption that prices will keep falling.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告不要想当然地认为物价会持续下跌。

dict_mnemonic.text: as（去）+ sum（拿）+ ption（名词）——伸手把东西拿进自己怀里；谐音“额萨姆普申”：额（我）萨姆（sum）普（p）申（tion）手，把前提揽过来 → assumption 假设；承担

root: 源自拉丁语 assumere（ad-“向”+ sumere“拿取”，sumere 又由 sub-“在下”+ emere“取”构成），经古法语 assumpcion 进入英语；-tion 为动作名词后缀，核心是“把某物拿起来、揽到自己身上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one reach. The hand takes up a proposition, then a duty, then a seat of office, then what was never offered, then a false face; the church finally takes a body up into heaven.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一次伸手。手先拿起一个命题，再拿起一份责任、一个职位、一件从没被递过来的东西、一副假面孔；最后教会把一具身体接上了天。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: taking something up and drawing it to oneself — the hand's gesture applied to facts, duties, offices, and rights.
core.cn: 核心意象：把某物拿起来并拉到怀里——手的动作被用在事实、责任、职位和权利上。

branches.en: THE PROPOSITION: taken as given in daily reasoning, and set as the floor of a formal argument.
branches.cn: 命题：在日常推理中被当作已定，在正式论证中被当作地板。

branches.en: TAKING TOO MUCH: the unchecked guess, and the puffed-up manner of one who has taken too much.
branches.cn: 拿得太多：未经检验的猜测，以及揽得太多之人摆出的傲慢姿态。

branches.en: THE BURDEN AND THE SEAT: a duty taken onto the shoulders, an office taken into the hands.
branches.cn: 重担与座位：接到肩上的责任，接到手里的职位。

branches.en: TAKING WITHOUT LEAVE: a right seized, and an appearance put on like a garment.
branches.cn: 未经许可的拿取：被抢占的权利，以及像衣服一样披上的神情。

branches.en: THE ASSUMPTION: the one taking-up that is done to a person rather than by her.
branches.cn: 圣母升天：唯一一次不是本人拿取，而是被接上去的“拿起”。

intro.en: Assumption is assume plus -tion, a noun-of-action ending from Latin -tionem. Assume is ad- plus sum-, and sum- itself is sub- plus emere 'take'. The suffix adds nothing but the act; all the meaning lives in the direction of the taking.
intro.cn: assumption 是 assume 加 -tion，这个动作名词后缀来自拉丁语 -tionem。assume 是 ad- 加 sum-，而 sum- 本身又是 sub- 加 emere“取”。后缀只添加“动作”，全部意义都活在“拿取的方向”里。

latinIntro.en: Latin emere 'take' gives sumere 'take up' and, through its participle sumpt-, a whole family: assume, consume, resume, presume, subsume, and the expensive sumptuous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 emere“取”给出 sumere“拿起”，又通过分词词干 sumpt- 给出一整个词族：assume、consume、resume、presume、subsume，以及表示昂贵的 sumptuous。

items.meaning: to take to oneself; to suppose; to put on
items.meaningCN: 承担；假定；装出（拿到自己身上）
items.example: Do not assume that silence means consent.
items.exampleCN: 不要以为沉默就是同意。

items.meaning: the act of taking up; a thing taken for granted
items.example: The argument collapses without that assumption.
items.exampleCN: 没有那个假设，论证就垮了。

items.meaning: to take up completely; to use up
items.example: The factory consumes vast amounts of water.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂消耗大量水。

items.meaning: the using up of goods or energy
items.example: Energy consumption fell after the retrofit.
items.exampleCN: 改造之后能耗下降了。

items.meaning: to take up again
items.meaningCN: 重新开始；恢复（再次拿起）
items.example: Talks resumed after a week of silence.
items.exampleCN: 沉默一周后，谈判重新开始。

items.meaning: to take beforehand; to suppose with confidence
items.meaningCN: 推定；冒昧地假定（预先拿定）
items.example: I presume you have read the file.
items.exampleCN: 我想你已经读过那份文件了。

items.meaning: a belief taken in advance; boldness
items.example: It was a presumption to speak for the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 代表整个团队发言，是一种冒昧。

items.meaning: to take something under a larger category
items.example: The new rules subsume the older ones.
items.exampleCN: 新规则把旧规则囊括其中。

items.meaning: costly, lavish, as of a meal
items.example: They were received in a sumptuous hall.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一座奢华的大厅里受到接待。

items.meaning: not putting oneself forward; modest
items.example: An unassuming scholar corrected the whole field.
items.exampleCN: 一位谦逊的学者纠正了整个领域。

latinEntries.meaning: to take up, take to oneself

definition_zh: 保证；把握；自信；安心；保险；质量保证；厚颜
definition_en: a making sure, whether by a promise that removes doubt, a state of certainty, a policy against loss, or too much confidence in oneself
core_image: 一个人把手按在另一个人的肩上，说一声“放心”——把对方心里的不安换成确定
scene: At a kitchen table a father promises his daughter he will be there; in an office a clerk sells a life policy; a young man walks into an interview as if the job were already his. One word covers all three kinds of sure-ness. The father's promise to his daughter is an assurance that he will be there.
sceneCN: 这里 assurance 是「保证」（第 1 个义项：旨在使某人安心的郑重承诺）；句意：厨房桌边，父亲向女儿保证他一定会到，这句承诺就是一个保证。场景要点：厨房桌、父亲与女儿、寿险文件、面试门口。

senses.title: A word given to remove doubt
senses.titleCN: 保证：一句话把疑虑拿掉
senses.definition: a formal or solemn promise meant to give someone confidence
senses.definitionCN: 旨在使某人安心的正式或郑重承诺
senses.example: The company gave an assurance that no jobs would be cut.
senses.exampleCN: 公司保证不会裁员。
senses.why: Late 14c., 'formal or solemn pledge, promise', from Old French asseurance. The noun of -ance names the act of making sure, and a promise is the cheapest instrument for making another mind sure.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪末的“正式或郑重承诺”来自古法语 asseurance。这个 -ance 名词命名“使确定”的动作，而承诺是使另一颗心确定起来最便宜的工具。

senses.title: Certainty in the mind
senses.titleCN: 把握：心里再无怀疑的那种确定
senses.definition: full confidence or certainty that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 对某事为真或将会发生的充分信心或确定
senses.example: She spoke with the assurance of someone who had checked every figure.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话时带着一种查过每个数字的人才有的把握。
senses.why: The same late 14c. entry also meant 'certainty, full confidence'. The noun names both the act of making sure and the state of being sure, because -ance can take either side of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 14 世纪末的词条还兼指“确定、充分信心”。这个名词既命名“使确定”的动作，也命名“已确定”的状态，因为 -ance 可以取动词的两面。

senses.title: Carrying yourself as if you cannot fail
senses.titleCN: 自信：走起路来像不会失败
senses.definition: self-confidence, especially in manner or bearing
senses.definitionCN: 自信，尤指态度或举止上的
senses.example: Years of stage work gave her a quiet assurance.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的舞台经历给了她一种安静的自信。
senses.why: The sense 'self-confident' is recorded from the 1590s. Making others sure of you turns inward: the same act now has one's own self as its object.
senses.whyCN: “自信”义记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。使别人对你确定，转向了内部：同一个动作，如今对象成了自己。

senses.title: The calm that follows being told
senses.titleCN: 安心：被告知之后的那口气
senses.definition: a feeling of relief and freedom from worry produced by a promise or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 因承诺或解释而获得的宽慰、免于忧虑之感
senses.example: His assurance that the train would wait let her breathe again.
senses.exampleCN: 他保证火车会等，这才让她重新喘上气来。
senses.why: The verb assure meant 'reassure, give confidence to' from late 14c. Latin securus is literally 'free from care' (se- 'without' + cura 'care'), so assurance names the removal of care rather than the promise that removes it.
senses.whyCN: 动词 assure 从 14 世纪末就意为“使安心、给信心”。拉丁语 securus 字面是“无忧”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”），所以 assurance 命名的是忧虑被拿掉，而不是拿掉它的那句承诺。

senses.title: A policy against loss
senses.titleCN: 保险：用一笔钱买下“不会损失”
senses.definition: insurance, especially life insurance (British usage)
senses.definitionCN: 保险，尤指人寿保险（英式用法）
senses.example: He took out a life assurance policy when his first child was born.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个孩子出生时，他买了一份人寿保险。
senses.why: Assurance was the older English word for commercial insurance from the late 16c.; insurance, its en- variant, took over in the 1650s. A premium buys a written promise that loss will be made sure against.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪末起，assurance 就是商业保险较早的英语说法；它的 en- 变体 insurance 在 17 世纪 50 年代接手。保费买下的是一纸承诺：损失会被“确保”抵挡。

senses.title: Quality made certain by process
senses.titleCN: 质量保证：靠流程把质量做成确定
senses.definition: the part of a business that systematically checks that products meet a standard
senses.definitionCN: 企业系统检查产品是否符合标准的部分
senses.example: Quality assurance caught the fault before the parts left the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 质量保证在零件出厂前就查出了缺陷。
senses.why: Twentieth-century industry moved assurance from a spoken promise to a procedure: instead of assuring a customer in words, a firm builds certainty into every step. The abstract noun becomes the name of a department.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的工业把 assurance 从口头承诺变成流程：企业不再用话向客户保证，而是把确定性做进每一道工序。抽象名词于是成了一个部门的名称。

senses.title: A guarantee that something holds
senses.titleCN: 保障：保证某件事站得住
senses.definition: a guarantee that something exists, continues, or is adequate
senses.definitionCN: 对某物存在、持续或足够充分的保证
senses.example: The treaty offers an assurance of water supply to the lower valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约为下游河谷提供了供水保障。
senses.why: Here assurance is followed by of rather than that: the noun names the thing made certain, not the sentence spoken. It is the same 'making sure', shifted from a hearer's mind to a fact in the world.
senses.whyCN: 这里 assurance 后接 of 而不是 that：名词命名的是被确保的那件事，而不是说出的那句话。还是同一个“使确定”，只是从听者的心里移到了世上的一个事实。

senses.title: Too much sureness of oneself
senses.titleCN: 厚颜：对自己太有把握
senses.definition: impudence or presumption in manner (18th-century shading, now rare)
senses.definitionCN: 举止上的放肆、冒昧（18 世纪色彩，今罕用）
senses.example: He had the assurance to ask for a raise in his first week.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟有脸在上班第一周就要求加薪。
senses.why: The word had a negative tinge in the 18c., often suggesting impudence or presumption. There is a point where being sure of oneself stops looking like calm and starts looking like a claim on others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 18 世纪带有贬义色彩，常指放肆或冒昧。对自己有把握，到某一点就不再像从容，而像对别人提要求。

senses.title: The deed that makes a right sure
senses.titleCN: 担保契据：让权利站得住的那张纸
senses.definition: a formal deed or clause that makes a right, title, or payment certain (legal)
senses.definitionCN: 使权利、所有权或付款成为确定的正式契据或条款（法律）
senses.example: The solicitor prepared an assurance of the title for the buyer.
senses.exampleCN: 律师为买方准备了一份产权担保契据。
senses.why: English -ance nouns often name the instrument as well as the act. In conveyancing an assurance is the deed that makes a title sure, just as a promise makes a mind sure.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -ance 名词常同时命名动作和凭据。在不动产转让中，assurance 就是让产权站得住的那张契据，正如承诺让一颗心站得住。

intro.en: Assurance is assure plus -ance. Assure came through Old French asseurer from Vulgar Latin *assecurar, ad- 'to' plus securus 'free from care'; -ance makes an abstract noun of the act or state. The shift runs from 'making someone care-free' to 'a pledge', to 'certainty', to 'self-confidence', and finally to 'insurance'.
intro.cn: assurance 是 assure 加 -ance。assure 经古法语 asseurer 来自俗拉丁语 *assecurar，即 ad-“向”加 securus“无忧”；-ance 把动作或状态变成抽象名词。语义从“使某人无忧”走到“承诺”，再到“确定”“自信”，最后到“保险”。

items.en: Securus meant 'free from care, safe, secure', built from se- 'without, apart' plus cura 'care, anxiety'. The adjective describes a person, not a lock: to be secure is to have no care in the mind.
items.cn: securus 意为“无忧的、安全的、稳固的”，由 se-“无、离开”加 cura“忧虑、照料”构成。这个形容词描述的是人，不是锁：secure 就是心里没有忧虑。

items.en: The verb *assecurar, ad- plus securus, meant 'to make free from care'. The starred form is a reconstruction with no written record, so its exact shape is marked source uncertain; only its descendants in French and English are attested.
items.cn: 动词 *assecurar 由 ad- 加 securus 构成，意为“使无忧”。带星号的形式是没有书面记录的重构，因此其确切形态标为“来源不确定”；只有它在法语和英语中的后裔有文献可证。

items.en: Asseurer meant 'to reassure, calm, protect, to render sure', and the noun asseurance (11c.) meant 'assurance, promise; truce; certainty, safety, security'. Old French had already spread the word across trust, calm, and safety.
items.cn: asseurer 意为“使安心、使平静、保护、使确定”，名词 asseurance（11 世纪）意为“保证、承诺；停战；确定、安全、稳固”。古法语已经把这个词铺展到信任、平静与安全三个方面。

items.en: Assurance enters English as both 'formal or solemn pledge, promise' and 'certainty, full confidence'. Assure follows in the same period, meaning 'reassure, give confidence to; make secure; bind by a pledge'.
items.cn: assurance 进入英语时兼有“正式或郑重承诺”与“确定、充分信心”两义。assure 也在同一时期出现，意为“使安心、给信心；使安全；以承诺约束”。

items.en: 'Self-confident' is recorded from the 1590s. In the 18c. the word took a negative tinge, often suggesting impudence or presumption: too much assurance became a social fault.
items.cn: “自信”义记录于 16 世纪 90 年代。到 18 世纪，这个词带上贬义色彩，常指放肆或冒昧：过多的 assurance 成了一种社交过失。

items.en: Assurance was the older term for commercial insurance from the late 16c.; insurance, its en- variant, became standard in the 1650s. In the 20c. quality assurance turned the promise into a procedure, and the word acquired its modern office meaning.
items.cn: 从 16 世纪末起，assurance 是商业保险的较早说法；它的 en- 变体 insurance 在 17 世纪 50 年代成为标准。20 世纪，quality assurance 把承诺变成流程，这个词又添了现代的企业部门义。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on sure/secur-: insurance and reassure are true relatives with different prefixes. Endurance merely rhymes in shape and comes from durus 'hard', so it must be kept apart.
note.cn: 形近组建立在 sure/secur- 上：insurance 与 reassure 都是换前缀的真同族。endurance 只是外形相押，来自 durus“坚硬”，必须分开。

entries.tag: en- variant of the same word
entries.definition: cover against loss in exchange for payment. It is the en- twin of assurance and now the standard commercial term.
entries.definitionCN: 以付费换取损失保障。它是 assurance 的 en- 双胞胎，如今是标准的商业术语。

entries.definition: to make someone sure or free from doubt. Assurance is the state or act that the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人确定、使免于疑虑。assurance 是这动词所产生的状态或行为。

entries.definition: comfort given to remove fear a second time. It repeats the making-sure with re-.
entries.definitionCN: 再次消除恐惧的安慰。它用 re- 重复了“使确定”这个动作。

entries.definition: the power to bear hardship, from durus 'hard'. The -ance ending is shared, the root is not.
entries.definitionCN: 忍耐力，来自 durus“坚硬”。词尾 -ance 相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: a promise that something will be done or will work. It is the most enforceable synonym of assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事将做到或能奏效的承诺。它是 assurance 最具可执行性的同义词。

entries.definition: a serious promise, often with something given as security. It matches the formal tone of assurance.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重的承诺，常以某物作担保。它对应 assurance 的正式语气。

entries.definition: the quality of being definitely true or known. It is assurance as a state of mind or fact.
entries.definitionCN: 确定无疑的性质。它是作为心理或事实状态的 assurance。

entries.definition: belief in one's own or another's ability. It overlaps assurance in both the self and the promise senses.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己或他人能力的信任。它在“自信”和“可托付”两层上都与 assurance 重叠。

entries.definition: a written promise that goods will be repaired or replaced. It is assurance limited to a product.
entries.definitionCN: 对商品将维修或更换的书面承诺。它是被限定在商品上的 assurance。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: ad- 'to', securus 'free from care', -ance 'state of'. Assurance is literally the act of putting someone beyond care.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：ad-“向”、securus“无忧”、-ance“状态”。assurance 字面上就是把某人放到忧虑之外。

normal.en: assurance = as- (ad-, 'to') + sure ('certain') + -ance: making someone certain.
normal.cn: assurance = as-（ad-，“向”）+ sure（“确定”）+ -ance：使某人确定。

normal.en: The sure family runs through assure, reassure, ensure, insure, and secure.
normal.cn: sure 词族贯穿 assure、reassure、ensure、insure、secure。

normal.en: Insurance is the en- twin of assurance: same promise, different prefix.
normal.cn: insurance 是 assurance 的 en- 双胞胎：同一个承诺，不同的前缀。

normal.en: Quality assurance is a promise turned into a checklist.
normal.cn: quality assurance 是被做成了检查表的承诺。

normal.en: To speak with assurance is to sound as if your words had already been checked.
normal.cn: speak with assurance，就是听起来像你的话已经被核对过了。

abstract.en: Sureness is pictured as a weight lifted off the chest: securus is literally 'without care'.
abstract.cn: “确定”被画成从胸口搬走的一块重物：securus 字面就是“没有忧虑”。

abstract.en: The word travels from the hearer's mind to the speaker's manner: first you calm him, then you look calm yourself.
abstract.cn: 这个词从听者的心里走到说者的姿态：先让他安定，再让自己看起来安定。

abstract.en: A promise, a policy, and a deed are three ways of writing the same sentence: this will not fail you.
abstract.cn: 一句承诺、一份保单、一张契据，是同一句话的三种写法：它不会辜负你。

examples.en: The minister refused to give any assurance about the timing of the vote.
examples.cn: 部长拒绝就投票时间作出任何保证。

examples.en: She answered the hostile questions with the assurance of a practised speaker.
examples.cn: 她以老练演讲者的自信回答了那些敌意提问。

examples.en: In Britain, life assurance is often sold alongside a mortgage.
examples.cn: 在英国，人寿保险常与按揭一起销售。

dict_mnemonic.text: as（去）+ sure（确定）+ ance（名词）——去把“确定”给他，就是保证；谐音“额秀润斯”：额（我）秀（sure）润（ance）——拍胸脯让他放心 → assurance 保证；自信

root: 源自拉丁语 securus“无忧的”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”），经俗拉丁语 *assecurar、古法语 asseurer 进入英语；-ance 为抽象名词后缀，核心是“使某人心里无忧、确定”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one removal of care. A promise takes doubt out of another mind; certainty and self-confidence keep it out of one's own; insurance and quality assurance sell the removal; and too much of it turns into impudence.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一次“拿走忧虑”。承诺把疑虑从别人心里拿走；确定与自信把它从自己心里拿走；保险与质量保证把这次“拿走”拿来出售；而拿走得太多，就变成了厚颜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: making someone care-free — a hand on the shoulder, a word given, a policy signed.
core.cn: 核心意象：使某人无忧——一只手按在肩上，一句话给出，一份保单签下。

branches.en: THE PROMISE AND THE CALM: the word given, and the relief it leaves in the hearer.
branches.cn: 承诺与安心：给出的那句话，以及它在听者心里留下的宽慰。

branches.en: CERTAINTY AND SAFEGUARD: a fact held sure in the mind, and a fact made sure in the world.
branches.cn: 确定与保障：在心里被拿稳的事实，以及在世上被确保的事实。

branches.en: SELF-ASSURANCE: the calm of the capable, sliding into the impudence of the over-sure.
branches.cn: 自信：能者的从容，滑向过度自信者的放肆。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL FORMS: a policy sold against loss, a procedure built to prevent it.
branches.cn: 制度化形态：为抵御损失而卖的保单，为预防损失而建的流程。

branches.en: THE DEED: the same making-sure written down and sealed.
branches.cn: 契据：同一个“使确定”被写下来并盖了章。

intro.en: Assurance is assure plus -ance. Assure is ad- plus the sure/secur- base, so the word is prefix, root, and abstract ending in that order. The ending lets the same noun mean the act of assuring and the state of being assured.
intro.cn: assurance 是 assure 加 -ance。assure 是 ad- 加 sure/secur- 词根，所以整词依次是前缀、词根、抽象后缀。后缀让同一个名词既能指“使确定”的动作，也能指“已确定”的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus 'free from care' (se- 'without' + cura 'care') is the root of sure, secure, security, assure, assurance, insure and insurance. The prefixes ad-, re-, in-, en- each redirect the same 'care-free' idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus“无忧”（se-“无”+ cura“忧虑”）是 sure、secure、security、assure、assurance、insure、insurance 的词根。前缀 ad-、re-、in-、en- 各自把同一个“无忧”观念转向不同方向。

items.meaning: to make someone free from doubt
items.example: He assured her that the door had been locked.
items.exampleCN: 他向她保证门已经锁好了。

items.meaning: a pledge; certainty; insurance
items.example: She needed an assurance before she signed.
items.exampleCN: 签字之前她需要一个保证。

items.meaning: to calm someone's fear again
items.example: The doctor reassured the family.
items.exampleCN: 医生让家属安了心。

items.meaning: certain, convinced
items.example: Are you sure the key is in your bag?
items.exampleCN: 你确定钥匙在你包里吗？

items.meaning: safe; free from anxiety
items.example: The documents are secure in the vault.
items.exampleCN: 文件在保险库里很安全。

items.meaning: the state of being safe
items.example: Airport security has been tightened.
items.exampleCN: 机场安保已经加强。

items.meaning: to make certain against loss by paying
items.example: They insured the painting for two million.
items.exampleCN: 他们为这幅画投保了两百万。

items.meaning: cover bought against loss
items.example: The policy includes travel insurance.
items.exampleCN: 这份保单包含旅行保险。

items.meaning: to make something certain to happen
items.example: Please ensure that the window is closed.
items.exampleCN: 请确保窗户关好。

items.meaning: certain; guaranteed
items.example: An assured income let him write full time.
items.exampleCN: 一份有保障的收入让他能全职写作。

definition_zh: 附件；附着物；连接；依恋；忠诚；扣押；派驻；附着
definition_en: the act or state of being fastened to something, and the thing, feeling, or legal claim that is fastened
core_image: 一件东西被钉住、拴在另一件东西上；后来是人把心拴在某人身上，法院把财产拴在判决上
scene: A clerk clips a receipt to an invoice; a child refuses to leave her grandmother's side; a bailiff nails a notice to a warehouse door. Fastening, feeling, and seizing turn out to be one verb. The receipt clipped to the invoice is an attachment to it.
sceneCN: 这里 attachment 是「附件」（第 1 个义项：随文件附上的东西）；句意：职员把收据夹在发票上，这张收据就是发票的附件。场景要点：收据、发票、夹子、奶奶与孩子、仓库门上的通知。

senses.title: The file clipped to the message
senses.titleCN: 附件：夹在消息后面的那个文件
senses.definition: a file sent with an email or fastened to a document
senses.definitionCN: 随电子邮件发送或附在文件上的文件
senses.example: The report is in the attachment, not in the body of the email.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在附件里，不在邮件正文中。
senses.why: The sense 'something attached to something else' dates from 1797 and became dominant with electronic mail. The metaphor is clerical: a sheet physically clipped behind a letter.
senses.whyCN: “附在另一物上的东西”这一义始于 1797 年，并在电子邮件时代成为主导义。它的隐喻是文书式的：一张纸被夹在信件后面。

senses.title: The part added to the whole
senses.titleCN: 附着物：后来加装到整机上的那个部件
senses.definition: an accessory or extra part fitted to a machine or device
senses.definitionCN: 加装在机器或设备上的配件或附加部件
senses.example: The drill comes with three attachments for different surfaces.
senses.exampleCN: 这把电钻配有三个适用于不同表面的附件。
senses.why: From the same 1797 'thing attached', narrowed in engineering to a part that hangs on the main body. It is not essential to the whole, only fastened to it.
senses.whyCN: 同样来自 1797 年“被附上的东西”，在工程语境里窄化为挂在主体上的部件。它对整体并非必需，只是被固定在上面。

senses.title: The act of fastening
senses.titleCN: 连接：把两样东西钉在一起的动作
senses.definition: the act or state of being joined or fastened to something
senses.definitionCN: 被连接或固定到某物上的动作或状态
senses.example: The attachment of the trailer took less than a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 挂上拖车用了不到一分钟。
senses.why: Attach is recorded c.1400 as 'fasten, affix, connect', which is probably the original etymological sense. The noun simply names that act, before any of its specialized meanings.
senses.whyCN: attach 在约 1400 年记录为“固定、附上、连接”，这大概就是它词源上的本义。名词只是命名这个动作，早于它所有专门化的义项。

senses.title: A heart fastened to another
senses.titleCN: 依恋：把心拴在另一个人身上
senses.definition: a strong feeling of affection or fondness for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的强烈喜爱或眷恋
senses.example: The child's attachment to her old teddy bear survived every move.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子对旧泰迪熊的依恋历经每次搬家都没消失。
senses.why: The meaning 'sympathy, devotion' is recorded from 1704. The physical bond is simply transferred to feeling: what cannot be seen is described as a fastening of the heart.
senses.whyCN: “同情、挚爱”义记录于 1704 年（18 世纪初）。物理的联结被直接转到情感上：看不见的东西，被描述成心被拴住。

senses.title: Loyalty fastened to a cause
senses.titleCN: 忠诚：把归属拴在一个事业上
senses.definition: loyalty or devotion to a group, cause, or belief
senses.definitionCN: 对某个群体、事业或信念的忠诚与忠贞
senses.example: His attachment to the reform movement never weakened.
senses.exampleCN: 他对改革运动的忠诚从未减弱。
senses.why: Once devotion could be fastened to a person, it could be fastened to a party or an idea. The same noun serves the heart's bonds whether their object is a face or a cause.
senses.whyCN: 一旦挚爱可以拴在一个人身上，它也就可以拴在一个党派或一种理念上。同一个名词服务于心的各种联结，对象是一张脸或一项事业都一样。

senses.title: Seized so it cannot move
senses.titleCN: 扣押：让它动不了的“钉住”
senses.definition: the seizure of property or wages by legal order
senses.definitionCN: 依法律命令对财产或工资的扣押
senses.example: The court ordered the attachment of his bank account.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令扣押他的银行账户。
senses.why: The earliest English sense, c.1400, was 'arrest of a person on judicial warrant' (mid-13c. in Anglo-Latin); property, including wages, followed by the 1590s. Law fastens goods the way a nail fastens a door.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的义项（约 1400 年）是“依法拘押某人”（盎格鲁拉丁语中早至 13 世纪中叶）；对财产（后来包括工资）的扣押在 16 世纪 90 年代跟上。法律钉住财物，正如钉子钉住门。

senses.title: The order that authorizes the seizure
senses.titleCN: 扣押令：授权查封的那纸命令
senses.definition: a writ or court order authorizing the seizure of property or a person
senses.definitionCN: 授权扣押财产或拘押人的令状或法院命令
senses.example: The creditor obtained a writ of attachment against the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 债权人取得了针对该仓库的扣押令。
senses.why: The -ment noun can name the instrument as well as the act. Once a seizure required paper, the paper itself was called an attachment, like a nail that comes with its own hammer.
senses.whyCN: -ment 名词既能命名动作，也能命名凭据。扣押一旦需要文书，那张文书本身也就叫 attachment，像一颗自带锤子的钉子。

senses.title: A person fastened to another unit
senses.titleCN: 派驻：被临时拴到另一个单位的人
senses.definition: a temporary posting of a person to another unit, especially in the military or diplomatic service
senses.definitionCN: 人员临时派驻到另一单位，尤指军事或外交系统
senses.example: She spent six months on attachment to the defence ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她被借调到国防部六个月。
senses.why: In service language a person is attached, not transferred: the home unit keeps the strings while the officer works elsewhere. The noun records a fastening that is deliberately temporary.
senses.whyCN: 在军队与外交语言里，人是被 attach 而不是被 transfer：军官在别处工作，原单位仍握着那根线。这个名词记录的是刻意临时的“拴住”。

senses.title: A virus fastening to a cell
senses.titleCN: 附着：病毒钉在细胞表面的那一步
senses.definition: the binding of a substance, cell, or organism to a surface or another cell
senses.definitionCN: 物质、细胞或生物体结合到某一表面或另一细胞上
senses.example: Attachment to the host cell is the first step of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 附着到宿主细胞是感染的第一步。
senses.why: Twentieth-century biology reused the oldest physical sense without metaphor: a virus really does fasten to a receptor. The word returns to the nail and the post after its detour through feeling and law.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的生物学不加比喻地重新启用了最古老的物理义：病毒确实钉在受体上。这个词在情感与法律之间绕了一圈，又回到了钉子和桩。

intro.en: Attachment is attach plus -ment. Attach came through Old French atachier (earlier estachier) from a- 'to' plus a Germanic base probably meaning 'post, stake'. The -ment makes a noun of act or result, so the word covers the fastening, the thing fastened, and the feeling that imitates fastening.
intro.cn: attachment 是 attach 加 -ment。attach 经古法语 atachier（更早作 estachier）而来，由 a-“向”加一个可能意为“桩、柱”的日耳曼词干构成。-ment 造出表示动作或结果的名词，于是这个词覆盖了“固定”这个动作、被固定的东西，以及模仿固定的情感。

items.en: The base is usually traced to Frankish *stakon 'a post, stake', from Proto-Germanic *stakon- and PIE *steg- 'pole, stick'. The reconstruction has no written record and the connection is only probable, so this layer is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词干通常被追溯到法兰克语 *stakon“桩、柱”，来自原始日耳曼语 *stakon- 与印欧语 *steg-“杆、棍”。该重构没有书面记录，联系也只是或然的，因此这一层标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Estachier meant 'to attach, fix; stake up, support', later atachier 'fasten; arrest'. The earliest picture is agricultural or military: driving a stake into the ground to hold something upright.
items.cn: estachier 意为“附着、固定；用桩支起、支撑”，后来作 atachier“固定；拘押”。最早的画面是农业或军事的：把一根桩打进地里，让某物立住。

items.en: Attachement appears in Anglo-Latin as 'arrest of a person on judicial warrant'. The legal sense is the first one recorded for the word, which is why 'attachment' can still mean a seizure.
items.cn: attachement 在盎格鲁拉丁语中以“依法拘押某人”出现。法律义是这个词最早被记录的义项，所以 attachment 至今仍可指扣押。

items.en: Attach enters English as a legal term, 'to take or seize property or goods by law'. Only c.1400 does the etymologically older sense 'fasten, affix, connect' appear in English records.
items.cn: attach 作为法律术语进入英语：“依法取得或扣押财产、货物”。直到约 1400 年，词源上更古老的“固定、附上、连接”义才出现在英语记录里。

items.en: Attachment begins as 'arrest of a person on judicial warrant'. The application to property, including wages, is by the 1590s; the legal branch is thus older than the physical one in English.
items.cn: attachment 最初指“依法拘押某人”。它用于财产（后来包括工资）要到 16 世纪 90 年代；所以在英语里，法律分支比物理分支更老。

items.en: 'Sympathy, devotion' is recorded from 1704; 'something attached to something else' from 1797, which electronic mail later made everyday. The emotional sense is thus early 18c., not late 18c.
items.cn: “同情、挚爱”义记录于 1704 年（18 世纪初）；“附在另一物上的东西”义记录于 1797 年，后来被电子邮件变成日常用语。情感义属于 18 世纪初，而非 18 世纪末。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tach-/tach shape: detachment is the true opposite with de-, attaché is the same French verb in a person-noun. Attainment looks close but comes from tangere 'touch', so it is a false friend.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tach-/tach 的外形：detachment 是加 de- 的真正反义词，attaché 是同一个法语动词的人称名词。attainment 形似却来自 tangere“触碰”，是假朋友。

entries.definition: the act of separating, or a state of aloofness. It is attachment with de- 'away'.
entries.definitionCN: 分离；超然。它就是加了 de-“离开”的 attachment。

entries.definition: to fasten or join something to another. Attachment is the resulting state or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物固定或连接到另一物上。attachment 是随之而来的状态或东西。

entries.definition: the reaching of a goal, from ad- plus tangere 'touch'. It sounds like attachment but means touching a target, not fastening to it.
entries.definitionCN: 达到目标，来自 ad- 加 tangere“触碰”。它听起来像 attachment，意思是触到目标，而不是被固定在目标上。

entries.definition: a diplomatic official attached to an embassy. It is the person-noun made from the same French verb.
entries.definitionCN: 使馆随员。它是由同一个法语动词构成的人称名词。

entries.definition: a connection that holds people together. It is the emotional side of attachment without the physical image.
entries.definitionCN: 把人联结在一起的纽带。它是 attachment 的情感面，但不带物理意象。

entries.definition: a feeling of liking or love. It names the warmth, where attachment names the fastening.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱之情。它命名的是暖意，而 attachment 命名的是“拴住”。

entries.definition: an extra item that improves or completes something. It matches the machine sense of attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 起补充或完善作用的附加物件。它对应 attachment 的机器义。

entries.definition: something sent inside a letter or package. It is the postal cousin of an email attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 随信或包裹一同寄出的东西。它是电子邮件附件的邮政亲戚。

entries.definition: the taking of property by legal authority. It is the plain noun for the legal sense of attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 依法取得财产。它是 attachment 法律义的朴素名词。

normalIntro.en: The links are real: a- 'to', a Germanic stake base, -ment 'result'. The word begins as a stake driven in and ends as a heart tied down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：a-“向”、日耳曼语“桩”词干、-ment“结果”。这个词始于打进地里的桩，终于被拴住的心。

normal.en: attachment = at- (a-, 'to') + tach ('fasten') + -ment: the thing fastened on.
normal.cn: attachment = at-（a-，“向”）+ tach（“固定”）+ -ment：被固定在……上的东西。

normal.en: The tach- pair is a door: attach fastens, detach unfastens.
normal.cn: tach- 这对词像一扇门：attach 是钉上，detach 是拆下。

normal.en: An email attachment is a sheet clipped behind a letter, minus the paper.
normal.cn: 电子邮件附件就是夹在信后的一张纸，只是没有纸。

normal.en: An attachment order nails a person's property to a court case.
normal.cn: 扣押令把一个人的财产钉在一桩案子上。

normal.en: A diplomatic attaché is fastened to an embassy for a tour.
normal.cn: 外交随员是在一段任期内被“拴”在使馆的人。

abstract.en: The word's four lives — legal, physical, emotional, administrative — all describe one geometry: two things held at a single point.
abstract.cn: 这个词的四段生命——法律的、物理的、情感的、行政的——都在描述同一种几何：两样东西被固定在一个点上。

abstract.en: When feeling is described as fastening, love becomes a thing you cannot easily detach from.
abstract.cn: 当情感被描述成固定，爱就成了一件你难以拆卸的东西。

abstract.en: Attachment is always a relation, never a substance: there is no attachment without something to be attached to.
abstract.cn: attachment 永远是一种关系，而不是实体：没有可附着之物，就没有 attachment。

examples.en: Please open the attachment before the meeting; it contains the revised budget.
examples.cn: 请在会前打开附件，里面有修订后的预算。

examples.en: His attachment to the village grew stronger with every visit.
examples.cn: 每去一次，他对这个村子的依恋就更深一分。

examples.en: The court ordered the attachment of the company's assets.
examples.cn: 法院下令扣押这家公司的资产。

dict_mnemonic.text: at（去）+ tach（钉住）+ ment（名词）——把东西钉在另一件东西上；谐音“额塔奇门特”：额（我）塔奇（tach）门（ment）——把附件钉在门上 → attachment 附件；依恋

root: 源自中古英语 attach“依法扣押、固定”，经古法语 atachier/estachier 而来，其词干可能与日耳曼语 *stakon“桩、柱”有关（来源不确定）；-ment 为名词后缀，核心是“拴住、钉住”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one fastening. Law seizes first, then hands fasten paper, then a part fastens to a machine, then a heart fastens to a person, and biology quietly returns to the nail.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一次固定。法律先扣押，然后手把纸附上，再把部件装到机器上，再把心拴到一个人身上，最后生物学安静地回到那颗钉子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held at one point against something else — a stake, a clip, a claim, a heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物在一个点上被抵住、固定在另一物上——一根桩、一个夹子、一项请求权、一颗心。

chain: A PART ADDED TO A WHOLE

branches.en: PHYSICAL FASTENING: joining two things, and the binding of a virus to a cell.
branches.cn: 物理固定：把两样东西连起来，以及病毒结合到细胞上。

branches.en: THE THING FASTENED: a file clipped to a message, a part fitted to a machine.
branches.cn: 被固定之物：夹在消息上的文件，装在机器上的部件。

branches.en: THE BOND OF FEELING: fondness for a person, loyalty to a cause.
branches.cn: 情感纽带：对一个人的眷恋，对一项事业的忠诚。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLAIM: the seizure of property, and the writ that authorizes it.
branches.cn: 法律请求权：对财产的扣押，以及授权扣押的令状。

branches.en: THE TEMPORARY TIE: a person lent to another unit while the home unit keeps the string.
branches.cn: 临时拴系：人借给另一个单位，原单位仍握着那根线。

intro.en: Attachment is attach plus -ment. Attach is a- 'to' plus a Germanic stake base, probably *stakon. The -ment ending makes the noun of result, which is why the word can mean the act, the object, and the relationship.
intro.cn: attachment 是 attach 加 -ment。attach 是 a-“向”加一个日耳曼语“桩”词干，可能是 *stakon。-ment 词尾造出结果名词，所以这个词能同时指动作、物体和关系。

latinIntro.en: This word is not Latin but Gallo-Germanic: Old French atachier and Frankish *stakon. Its true relatives are French and English, not the Latin tach- words; attainment, from tangere 'touch', is a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词不是拉丁语而是高卢-日耳曼语：古法语 atachier 与法兰克语 *stakon。它真正的亲属是法语和英语，而不是拉丁语 tach- 词；attainment 来自 tangere“触碰”，是另一个词族。

items.meaning: to fasten or join to something
items.example: Attach the label to the outside of the case.
items.exampleCN: 把标签贴在箱子的外面。

items.meaning: the act of fastening; the thing fastened; fondness
items.example: The attachment came loose during the flight.
items.exampleCN: 那个附加装置在飞行中松开了。

items.meaning: to unfasten and separate
items.example: Detach the cable before you move the printer.
items.exampleCN: 搬打印机之前先把线拆下来。

items.meaning: separated; emotionally aloof
items.example: He watched the dispute with a detached calm.
items.exampleCN: 他带着一种超然的平静旁观这场争端。

items.meaning: the state of being separated; a separate unit
items.example: A small detachment guarded the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 一支小分遣队守卫着桥。

items.meaning: able to be fastened on
items.example: The lens is attachable to any phone.
items.exampleCN: 这个镜头可以装在任何手机上。

items.meaning: an official attached to an embassy
items.meaningCN: 使馆随员（被派附于使馆的人）
items.example: The cultural attaché arranged the exhibition.
items.exampleCN: 文化随员安排了这场展览。

items.meaning: a post driven into the ground
items.example: They tied the tent to a stake.
items.exampleCN: 他们把帐篷拴在一根桩上。

items.meaning: able to be taken off
items.example: The hood is detachable for cleaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个罩子可以拆下来清洗。

items.meaning: fastened; fond of; married
items.example: He is deeply attached to his students.
items.exampleCN: 他对学生们感情很深。

definition_zh: 达到；取得；抵达；成就；学识；造诣；学业成绩；达标指标
definition_en: the act of reaching or obtaining something through effort, and the achievement or level that results from it
core_image: 攀岩者的指尖终于触到岩壁顶端那条边——达到，就是努力伸长之后终于碰到目标的那一下
scene: An education minister holds up a chart and says: We measure attainment, but a child's curiosity never appears on the chart.
sceneCN: 这里 attainment 先用「学业成绩、达到水平」（第 7 个义项：教育测量中的达到程度），再暗含「成就、素养」；句意：我们测量学业成绩，但孩子的好奇心从不出现在图表上。画面里有折线图、成绩单和一支教鞭。

pos.zh: 达到；取得；成就；学识；学业成绩

derivatives.zh: 无法达到的；高不可攀的

senses.title: The act of reaching
senses.titleCN: 达到：把努力伸到目标上
senses.definition: the act of reaching something that has been the object of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力而触及某个目标的行为
senses.example: The attainment of fluency in a second language takes years of daily practice.
senses.exampleCN: 第二语言流利程度的达到需要多年每日练习。
senses.why: -ment names the act, as in movement and payment; attain goes back to ad- 'to' + tangere 'touch'. The act is imagined as contact: you do not merely want the goal, you stretch until you touch it.
senses.whyCN: -ment 像 movement、payment 一样把动词变成「行为」；attain 出自 ad-「向」+ tangere「触碰」。这个行为被想象成一次接触：不是只想要目标，而是一直伸到碰着它。

senses.title: Arriving at a place
senses.titleCN: 抵达：脚终于踩到终点
senses.definition: the act of arriving at a place or at the end of a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地或走完一段旅程的行为
senses.example: The attainment of the summit came after nine hours of climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 在攀登九个小时之后，他们抵达了顶峰。
senses.why: Latin attingere meant both 'to touch' and 'to arrive at': a ship touches shore, a climber touches rock. English kept the literal spatial sense beside the figurative one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 attingere 既指「触碰」，也指「到达」：船靠岸是 touch，登山者碰着岩壁也是 touch。英语把字面的空间义和比喻义一并保留下来。

senses.title: Making a goal real
senses.titleCN: 实现：让目标落地
senses.definition: the successful bringing about of a goal, standard, or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 目标、标准或协议的顺利实现
senses.example: The attainment of the treaty took two years of quiet diplomacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份条约的达成用了两年安静的外交斡旋。
senses.why: The object of attaining can be abstract; a standard or an agreement is 'reached' once its conditions are met. The spatial metaphor is extended to anything with a threshold.
senses.whyCN: attain 的宾语可以是抽象物；标准或协议的条件一满足，就算「够到了」。这个空间比喻被推广到一切有门槛的事物。

senses.title: Obtaining a right or status
senses.titleCN: 取得：拿到资格或身份
senses.definition: the obtaining of a right, qualification, or status, especially in formal use
senses.definitionCN: 权利、资格或身份的获得，尤用于正式语境
senses.example: Attainment of citizenship requires five years of residence.
senses.exampleCN: 取得公民身份需要居住满五年。
senses.why: Official English uses attainment for entering a status: citizenship, majority, a qualification. The status is treated as a place, and its conditions are the road that leads there.
senses.whyCN: 正式英语用 attainment 表示进入某种身份：公民资格、成年、资历。身份被当成一个地点，条件则是通往那里的路。

senses.title: A thing achieved
senses.titleCN: 成就：够下来的那件东西
senses.definition: an achievement or accomplishment, especially one won by sustained effort
senses.definitionCN: 尤指靠持续努力赢得的成就或业绩
senses.example: His greatest attainment was the bridge that still carries traffic today.
senses.exampleCN: 他最大的成就是那座至今仍在通车的桥。
senses.why: From the 1670s the noun also named the thing at the end of effort, not the effort itself. Since -ment can denote a result (as in 'a payment'), the touch became a possession.
senses.whyCN: 从 17 世纪 70 年代起，这个名词也指努力尽头的那件东西，而不只是努力本身。-ment 能表示结果（如 a payment），于是那一下触碰变成了一份所有物。

senses.title: Learned skill, usually plural
senses.titleCN: 学识：已经收进身体里的东西
senses.definition: a level of knowledge or skill in a subject, especially when impressive or scholarly
senses.definitionCN: 某一学科的知识或技能水平，尤指令人印象深刻或具学术性的
senses.example: She is a scholar of great attainments in medieval history.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位在中世纪史方面造诣很深的学者。
senses.why: The plural shifted the image from the act to the height reached: knowledge is what remains after the climb. The usage is slightly formal and old-fashioned, suited to praising a scholar.
senses.whyCN: 复数把意象从「动作」转到「达到的高度」：知识是攀登之后留在身上的东西。这种用法略正式、偏旧，适合称赞学者。

senses.title: Measured school level
senses.titleCN: 学业水平：把高度画成刻度
senses.definition: a pupil's measured level of knowledge, as recorded in school assessments
senses.definitionCN: 学生在学校评估中记录的知识水平
senses.example: Boys in the sample showed lower attainment in reading than girls.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中的男孩在阅读上表现出的学业水平低于女孩。
senses.why: Twentieth-century education made the height measurable: attainment became a score along a scale, used to compare groups. A metaphor of distance turned into a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的教育把这个高度变成可测量的东西：attainment 成了刻度上的分数，用来比较群体。距离的比喻由此变成统计数字。

senses.title: Attainment target
senses.titleCN: 达标指标：必须碰到的那条线
senses.definition: an official target set for pupils' or schools' results, used especially in British education
senses.definitionCN: 为学生或学校成绩设定的官方指标，尤用于英国教育
senses.example: The school narrowly missed its attainment target in mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以微弱差距未达到数学科的达标指标。
senses.why: British policy fixed 'attainment target' as an administrative phrase: the level a pupil or school is required to touch. The old image survives intact inside a government document.
senses.whyCN: 英国政策把 attainment target 固定为行政用语：学生或学校必须碰到的那条线。旧的意象原封不动地活在一份政府文件里。

senses.title: Something obtained
senses.titleCN: 取得物：努力留下的结果
senses.definition: something that has been obtained or brought into being as a result of effort
senses.definitionCN: 经努力而获得或产生的某物
senses.example: Clean water is an attainment that many villages still lack.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁的水是许多村庄至今仍未取得的一样东西。
senses.why: The result sense generalizes: anything brought into being by effort can be called an attainment, even an abstract good. Effort leaves a trace, and the trace takes the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 结果义进一步推广：任何靠努力产生的东西都能叫 attainment，哪怕是抽象的好事。努力留下痕迹，而这道痕迹沿用了动作的名字。

intro.en: Attainment is the noun of an old verb of touching. Latin tangere 'to touch' became attingere 'to reach by touching', French ataindre 'to reach', and English attain; the suffix -ment then turns the reaching into something nameable, countable and gradable.
intro.cn: attainment 是一个古老「触碰」动词的名词形式。拉丁语 tangere「触碰」变成 attingere「触而及之」，再变成法语 ataindre「达到」和英语 attain；后缀 -ment 又把「够到」变成可以命名、计数、评级的东西。

items.en: The root *tag- 'to touch, handle' is reconstructed from Latin tangere and its cognates. There is no written record of this layer, so it is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 *tag-「触碰、摆弄」是从拉丁语 tangere 及其同源词重构出来的。这一层没有书面记录，因此标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: Tangere 'to touch' formed attingere 'to touch; arrive at', from ad- 'to' + tangere. Latin already used the compound for 'attack, strike, manage', all felt as kinds of contact.
items.cn: tangere「触碰」构成 attingere「触及；到达」，由 ad-「向」+ tangere 组成。拉丁语已用它表示「攻击、打击、处理」，这些都被感受为不同方式的接触。

items.en: ataindre 'to come up to, reach, attain, strive' (Modern French atteindre) came from Vulgar Latin *attangere and supplied the stem ataign- that English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 ataindre「走近、达到、努力争取」（现代法语 atteindre）出自通俗拉丁语 *attangere，并提供了英语借入的词干 ataign-。

items.en: attain is recorded as 'succeed in reaching, come so near as to touch'. The borrowing belongs to the years around 1300, the period often described as the early 14th century.
items.cn: attain 被记录为「成功到达、近到可以触碰」。这一借入发生在 1300 年前后，也就是通常所说的 14 世纪初。

items.en: attainment enters through French atteignement as 'the action of acquiring by effort'. The suffix -ment names the act, as it does in payment and movement.
items.cn: attainment 经法语 atteignement 进入英语，意为「靠努力获取的行为」。后缀 -ment 命名动作，和 payment、movement 一样。

items.en: 'That which is attained, a personal accomplishment' is recorded from the 1670s. The plural attainments came to mean learned skill, and educational attainment and attainment target are 20th-century measurements.
items.cn: 「所达到之物、个人成就」记录于 17 世纪 70 年代。复数 attainments 后来指学术造诣，而 educational attainment 与 attainment target 是 20 世纪的测量用语。

note.en: The first group shares the -tainment ending or the tain/tang- root; the second group names results of effort that attainment can also denote.
note.cn: 第一组共享 -tainment 词尾或 tain/tang- 词根；第二组是 attainment 也能指称的各种努力成果。

entries.definition: to reach or obtain something by effort. It is the base of attainment, with the same tain/tang- root.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它是 attainment 的基础词，共享 tain/tang- 词根。

entries.definition: able to be reached or achieved. The -able suffix says the goal can be touched.
entries.definitionCN: 可达到的；可实现的。-able 后缀表示目标能够被够到。

entries.definition: the act of making amends, literally 'at-one-ment', from at + one. It is not related to attain.
entries.definitionCN: 赎罪；弥补，字面是 at-one-ment「成为一体」，由 at + one 构成，与 attain 不同源。

entries.definition: a reduction or lessening, from Old French abatre 'to beat down'. Only the -ment ending resembles attainment.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；减少，出自古法语 abatre「打倒」。只有 -ment 词尾与 attainment 相似。

entries.definition: a thing accomplished by effort, especially something notable. It matches the 'thing achieved' sense of attainment.
